sections.title: System, surroundings and the three types of system

board_events.text: System & Surroundings
System = the part of the universe under study. Surroundings = everything else that can trade energy or matter with it.
The boundary can be real (cooker wall) or purely imaginary.
Three types of system
OPEN: exchanges matter AND energy — open kadhai of boiling milk.
CLOSED: exchanges energy but NOT matter — sealed cooker before the whistle.
ISOLATED: exchanges NEITHER — hot chai in an ideal steel thermos.

segments.text: <curious>Let's start the way every scientist starts a thermodynamics problem — by drawing an imaginary boundary around just the piece of the world we actually care about.
Whatever sits inside that boundary is the system; everything outside it that can still trade energy or matter with it is the surroundings.
That boundary can be a real wall, like the side of a pressure cooker, or something purely imaginary that we simply agree to draw.
Now, depending on what the boundary allows through, we get exactly three kinds of system, and you meet all three in an ordinary kitchen.
An open system trades both matter and energy, like an open kadhai of boiling milk losing steam and heat at the same time.
A closed system lets energy through but not matter, like a sealed pressure cooker before the whistle blows, taking in heat while trapping every bit of steam.
And an isolated system trades nothing at all; the closest everyday picture is hot chai in a perfect steel thermos.
Here they are side by side, open, closed, and isolated, sorted purely by what their boundary is willing to let cross.
<curious>चलो शुरू करते हैं ठीक वैसे ही जैसे हर scientist एक thermodynamics problem शुरू करता है — उस हिस्से के चारों ओर एक imaginary boundary खींचकर जिसकी हमें सचमुच परवाह है।
इस boundary के अंदर जो कुछ है वही हमारा system है; और बाहर जो कुछ भी इसके साथ energy या matter exchange कर सकता है वही surroundings कहलाता है।
यह boundary एक असली दीवार हो सकती है, जैसे pressure cooker की दीवार, या फिर बिलकुल imaginary जिसे हम बस मान लेते हैं।
अब boundary किसको पार करने देती है इसके हिसाब से हमें ठीक तीन तरह के system मिलते हैं, और तीनों आपको एक आम रसोई में दिख जाते हैं।
एक open system matter और energy दोनों exchange करता है, जैसे उबलते दूध की खुली कढ़ाई जो steam और heat दोनों खोती रहती है।
एक closed system energy तो जाने देता है पर matter नहीं, जैसे whistle बजने से पहले वाला sealed pressure cooker जो heat लेता है पर हर बूँद steam अंदर रोक लेता है।
और एक isolated system कुछ भी exchange नहीं करता; इसका सबसे करीबी रोज़मर्रा का उदाहरण है perfect steel thermos में रखी गरम चाय।
यह रहे तीनों साथ में, open, closed, और isolated, सिर्फ़ इस बात पर छाँटे गए कि उनकी boundary क्या पार करने देती है।

sections.subtopic: Thermodynamic Terms, First Law, Internal Energy & Enthalpy
sections.title: State functions versus path functions

board_events.text: State function vs path function
Altitude gain on a hill depends only on start and finish — not the route. That is a STATE function.
Steps walked and water drunk depend on the route taken. Those are PATH functions.
Internal energy U and enthalpy H behave like altitude. Heat q and work w behave like steps.
Same start, same finish, different routes: two students always agree on the change in U, but may report different q and w.
Internal energy U = total kinetic + potential energy stored inside the system.
We can never measure absolute U — only the change in U is measurable.

segments.text: Here is the single most important habit of mind in this whole chapter, and it comes from a trek up to a hill temple.
Your altitude gain depends only on where you started and where you finished, never on whether you took the steep stairs or the winding road, so altitude is a state function.
But the number of steps you walked and the water you drank depend entirely on the route; those are path functions.
<excited>Internal energy and enthalpy behave exactly like altitude, while heat and work behave like steps walked.
So two students can take a gas from the same start to the same finish by totally different routes, and they will always agree on the change in internal energy, yet report different heat and work.
Physically, internal energy is just the grand total of every energy stored inside, the kinetic energy of jiggling molecules plus the potential energy locked in all their attractions and repulsions.
And here is the humbling fact: we can never pin down the absolute value of internal energy, only its change, just like a monthly change in a bank balance is easy even when the lifetime wealth is not.
The picture says it all: two routes, one honest altitude change at the ends.
यह इस पूरे chapter की सबसे ज़रूरी सोच है, और यह आती है एक पहाड़ी मंदिर की चढ़ाई से।
आपकी altitude gain सिर्फ़ इस पर निर्भर करती है कि आपने कहाँ से शुरू किया और कहाँ खत्म, इस पर नहीं कि आपने खड़ी सीढ़ियाँ लीं या घुमावदार रास्ता, इसलिए altitude एक state function है।
पर आपने कितने steps चले और कितना पानी पिया यह पूरी तरह रास्ते पर निर्भर करता है; वो path functions हैं।
<excited>Internal energy और enthalpy बिलकुल altitude जैसे behave करते हैं, जबकि heat और work steps walked जैसे।
तो दो students एक gas को एक ही start से एक ही finish तक अलग-अलग रास्तों से ले जा सकते हैं, और वे हमेशा internal energy के change पर सहमत होंगे, पर heat और work अलग बताएँगे।
Physically, internal energy अंदर जमा हर energy का कुल जोड़ है, हिलते molecules की kinetic energy और उनके सारे attractions-repulsions में बंद potential energy।
और यह रही humbling बात: हम internal energy की absolute value कभी नहीं नाप सकते, सिर्फ़ उसका change, ठीक जैसे bank balance का महीने भर का बदलाव आसान है पर ज़िंदगी भर की दौलत नहीं।
यह तस्वीर सब कह देती है: दो रास्ते, पर सिरों पर एक ही ईमानदार altitude change।

sections.subtopic: Thermodynamic Terms, First Law, Internal Energy & Enthalpy
sections.title: The first law and its sign convention

board_events.text: First law = energy conservation
Energy entering as heat or work must reappear as a change in internal energy — it cannot vanish or appear from nothing.
IUPAC / NCERT convention: q = heat supplied TO the system, w = work done ON the system.
$q \gt 0$ heat absorbed; $q \lt 0$ heat released.
$w \gt 0$ work done ON system (compression); $w \lt 0$ work done BY system (expansion).
Caution: heat and work are defined only for a PROCESS, never for a state. A gas does not 'contain' heat.

segments.text: The first law of thermodynamics sounds grand, but it is simply the law of energy conservation written in the language of systems.
Any energy that enters as heat or as work has to show up as a change in the internal energy; it cannot disappear and it cannot come from nowhere.
In symbols, the change in internal energy equals heat plus work, and this one line is the accounting rule for everything ahead.
The sign convention follows the I U P A C and N C E R T rule, viewed from the system's own point of view: q is heat supplied to the system, w is work done on the system.
So when q is positive the system absorbs heat, and when q is negative it releases heat.
<whisper>And here is the beat that trips up most students: positive work means work done on the system, that is compression, while negative work means work done by the system, that is expansion.
One last caution: heat and work are only defined for a process, for a change; it is meaningless to say a gas contains two hundred joules of heat, because a system stores internal energy, not heat.
First law of thermodynamics सुनने में भारी लगता है, पर यह बस energy conservation का नियम है जो systems की भाषा में लिखा गया है।
जो भी energy heat या work के रूप में अंदर आती है उसे internal energy के change के रूप में दिखना ही पड़ता है; वह न गायब हो सकती है, न कहीं से पैदा।
Symbols में, internal energy का change बराबर है heat plus work, और यही एक लाइन आगे की हर चीज़ का accounting rule है।
Sign convention I U P A C और N C E R T नियम से चलता है, system के अपने नज़रिए से: q है system को दी गई heat, और w है system पर किया गया work।
तो जब q positive है system heat absorb करता है, और जब q negative है वह heat release करता है।
<whisper>और यहीं ज़्यादातर students फँसते हैं: positive work का मतलब है system पर किया गया work, यानी compression, जबकि negative work यानी system द्वारा किया गया work, यानी expansion।

एक आखिरी सावधानी: heat और work सिर्फ़ किसी process के लिए, किसी change के लिए define होते हैं; यह कहना बेमानी है कि gas में two hundred joules heat है, क्योंकि system internal energy store करता है, heat नहीं।

sections.title: Reversible work, irreversible work and the cyclic process

board_events.text: Expansion work depends on the path
Gas pushes a piston out by change in V against external pressure. Work done ON the system is negative.
Reversible path: external pressure stays only infinitesimally below internal pressure at every step.
Reversible expansion extracts the MAXIMUM work: magnitude of reversible w exceeds magnitude of irreversible w.
Free expansion into vacuum: external pressure is zero, so w = 0.
Cyclic process: system returns to its start, so change in U over the cycle = 0.

board_events.caption: Area under the P-V curve is the work

segments.text: Why does work depend on the route while internal energy does not? Watch a gas push a piston.
As the gas expands by some volume against the outside pressure, it spends energy pushing the surroundings back, so the work done on the system comes out negative.
Now do the very same expansion reversibly, keeping the outside pressure only a hair below the inside pressure at every instant.

<curious>Because the gas is fighting the largest opposing pressure it possibly can at every step, the reversible route squeezes out the maximum work, and its magnitude beats the irreversible one between the same two states.
The opposite extreme is a free expansion into vacuum, where there is nothing to push against, so the work is exactly zero.
Now the elegant consequence: take the system all the way around a cycle back to its start, and because internal energy is a state function, its change over the full cycle is zero.
The first law then forces the net heat absorbed to equal the net work done by the system over the cycle, and this is precisely why heat and work can never be state functions.
On the P V diagram, the work is the area under the path, and you can literally see the reversible curve enclosing more area than the single irreversible step.
Work रास्ते पर क्यों निर्भर करता है जबकि internal energy नहीं? एक gas को piston धकेलते देखिए।
जैसे gas किसी volume तक बाहरी pressure के खिलाफ़ फैलती है, वह surroundings को पीछे धकेलने में energy खर्च करती है, इसलिए system पर किया गया work negative निकलता है।
अब वही expansion reversibly कीजिए, हर पल बाहरी pressure को अंदरूनी pressure से बस बाल भर नीचे रखते हुए।

<curious>क्योंकि gas हर step पर सबसे बड़े संभव opposing pressure से लड़ रही होती है, reversible रास्ता maximum work निचोड़ लेता है, और उसका magnitude उन्हीं दो states के बीच irreversible से ज़्यादा होता है।
इसका उल्टा छोर है vacuum में free expansion, जहाँ धकेलने को कुछ है ही नहीं, तो work बिलकुल zero होता है।
अब वो सुंदर नतीजा: system को पूरे cycle में घुमाकर वापस start पर लाइए, और चूँकि internal energy एक state function है, पूरे cycle पर उसका change zero होता है।
तब first law मजबूर कर देता है कि cycle पर net absorbed heat, system द्वारा किए गए net work के बराबर हो, और यही ठीक-ठीक वजह है कि heat और work कभी state functions नहीं हो सकते।
P V diagram पर work रास्ते के नीचे का area है, और आप साफ़ देख सकते हैं कि reversible curve single irreversible step से ज़्यादा area घेरती है।

segments.text: Let's collect the working formulas of the first subtopic on one board so you can jump straight here in revision.
The master statement is the first law: the change in internal energy equals heat plus work, both measured from the system's viewpoint.
For an expansion against a fixed outside pressure, the work is the simplest case.
Work on the system equals minus the external pressure times the change in volume; the minus sign is the expansion penalty we discussed.
When instead the gas expands reversibly and isothermally, we integrate over the path.
The reversible work equals minus n R T times the natural log of final over initial volume, which you may also write with two point three zero three times the log base ten.
<whisper>Reach instinctively for R equal to eight point three one four joules per kelvin per mole whenever the answer is wanted in joules, never the zero point zero eight two one value.
And do not forget the clean edge case: a free expansion into vacuum has zero external pressure, so the work is simply zero.
पहले subtopic के काम आने वाले formulas एक ही board पर इकट्ठा कर लेते हैं ताकि revision में आप सीधे यहीं आ सकें।
Master statement है first law: internal energy का change बराबर है heat plus work, दोनों system के नज़रिए से नापे गए।
किसी fixed बाहरी pressure के खिलाफ़ expansion के लिए work सबसे आसान case है।
System पर work बराबर है minus external pressure into change in volume; यह minus sign वही expansion penalty है जिसकी बात हमने की।
जब इसके बजाय gas reversibly और isothermally फैलती है, तो हम रास्ते भर integrate करते हैं।
Reversible work बराबर है minus n R T into natural log of final upon initial volume, जिसे आप two point three zero three into log base ten से भी लिख सकते हैं।
<whisper>जब भी answer joules में चाहिए, instinctively R बराबर eight point three one four joules per kelvin per mole उठाइए, कभी zero point zero eight two one नहीं।
और वो साफ़ edge case मत भूलिए: vacuum में free expansion का external pressure zero होता है, इसलिए work बस zero होता है।

sections.title: Enthalpy, the delta-H to delta-U bridge, and heat capacities

board_events.text: Enthalpy: heat content at constant pressure
Deriving the bridge from H = U + PV at constant T:
Delta n-g = (gaseous product moles) minus (gaseous reactant moles). Solids and liquids are NOT counted.
Heat exchanged under the two common constraints:

board_events.latex: C_P - C_V = R \quad (\text{ideal gas, per mole})

segments.text: Most reactions in the lab happen in open beakers at constant pressure, so chemists invented a quantity tailored to that situation: enthalpy.
Enthalpy is defined as internal energy plus the pressure-volume product, and like internal energy it is a state function whose absolute value we never need, only its change.
To connect enthalpy back to internal energy, start from that definition and change things at constant temperature and pressure.
For ideal gases this collapses to a beautifully usable bridge: the change in enthalpy equals the change in internal energy plus delta n-g times R T.

<curious>What is delta n-g? It is the moles of gaseous products minus the moles of gaseous reactants, and crucially, solids and liquids contribute negligible volume, so they are invisible to this term.
The two workhorse constraints come next, and they tell you which quantity a given experiment actually measures.
At constant volume the heat you measure is exactly the change in internal energy; at constant pressure it is exactly the change in enthalpy.
Finally, for an ideal gas per mole, the heat capacity at constant pressure exceeds that at constant volume by exactly R, Mayer's relation.
Lab में ज़्यादातर reactions खुले beakers में constant pressure पर होते हैं, इसलिए chemists ने उसी हालात के लिए बनी एक quantity ईजाद की: enthalpy।
Enthalpy को internal energy plus pressure-volume product के रूप में define करते हैं, और internal energy की तरह यह भी एक state function है जिसकी absolute value की ज़रूरत कभी नहीं, सिर्फ़ change की।
Enthalpy को वापस internal energy से जोड़ने के लिए, उसी definition से शुरू कीजिए और constant temperature व pressure पर बदलाव कीजिए।
Ideal gases के लिए यह एक बेहद काम के bridge में सिमट जाता है: enthalpy का change बराबर internal energy का change plus delta n-g into R T।
<curious>Delta n-g क्या है? यह gaseous products के moles minus gaseous reactants के moles है, और सबसे अहम, solids और liquids का volume नगण्य होता है, इसलिए इस term के लिए वे invisible हैं।
इसके बाद आते हैं दो workhorse constraints, जो बताते हैं कि कोई experiment असल में कौन सी quantity नापता है।
Constant volume पर आप जो heat नापते हैं वह ठीक internal energy का change है; constant pressure पर वह ठीक enthalpy का change है।
आखिर में, ideal gas के लिए per mole, constant pressure पर heat capacity, constant volume वाली से ठीक R ज़्यादा होती है, यही Mayer's relation है।

sections.subtopic: Thermodynamic Terms, First Law, Internal Energy & Enthalpy
sections.title: Applying the first law and the delta-H bridge

board_events.text: Example 1 (CBSE): find change in U
Flask absorbs 250 J of heat; in expanding it does 80 J of work on the surroundings.
q = +250 J; work done BY system, so w = -80 J.
Example 2 (NEET): delta-H from delta-U
1 mol gas becomes 2 mol at 300 K, change in U = +12.0 kJ, so delta n-g = +1.
Trap: use R = 8.314 (joules), keep T in kelvin, and since delta n-g = +1, delta-H exceeds delta-U.

segments.text: Let's put the first law to work with a clean C B S E-level example.
A sealed flask absorbs two hundred fifty joules of heat from a water bath, and while expanding it does eighty joules of work on its surroundings.
So q is plus two hundred fifty joules of heat absorbed, and because the work is done by the system, the work done on the system is minus eighty joules.
The first law gives the change in internal energy as two hundred fifty plus minus eighty, which is plus one hundred seventy joules; the heat input outweighs the energy spent pushing the surroundings.
Now a classic N E E T speed trap that links the change in enthalpy to the change in internal energy.
One mole of gas turns into two moles at three hundred kelvin with the change in internal energy at plus twelve kilojoules, so delta n-g is two minus one, that is plus one.
The bridge gives the change in enthalpy as twelve thousand plus one times eight point three one four times three hundred, roughly fourteen point five kilojoules.

<whisper>Watch the trap: reach for eight point three one four in joules, keep the temperature in kelvin, and since delta n-g is plus one, the change in enthalpy must exceed the change in internal energy.
First law को एक साफ़ C B S E-level example से काम में लगाते हैं।
एक sealed flask एक water bath से two hundred fifty joules heat absorb करता है, और फैलते हुए अपने surroundings पर eighty joules work करता है।
तो q है plus two hundred fifty joules absorbed heat, और चूँकि work system द्वारा किया गया है, system पर किया गया work minus eighty joules है।
First law से internal energy का change निकलता है two hundred fifty plus minus eighty, यानी plus one hundred seventy joules; heat input, surroundings को धकेलने में खर्च energy से ज़्यादा है।
अब एक classic N E E T speed trap जो enthalpy के change को internal energy के change से जोड़ता है।
One mole gas, three hundred kelvin पर two moles बन जाती है, internal energy का change plus twelve kilojoules के साथ, तो delta n-g है two minus one, यानी plus one।
Bridge से enthalpy का change निकलता है twelve thousand plus one into eight point three one four into three hundred, लगभग fourteen point five kilojoules।
<whisper>Trap देखिए: joules में eight point three one four उठाइए, temperature kelvin में रखिए, और चूँकि delta n-g plus one है, enthalpy का change internal energy के change से ज़्यादा होना ही चाहिए।

sections.subtopic: Thermodynamic Terms, First Law, Internal Energy & Enthalpy
sections.title: Isothermal reversible expansion and the path-dependence of work

board_events.text: Example 3 (JEE Main): isothermal reversible
2 mol ideal gas, 300 K, expands isothermally and reversibly from 5.0 L to 20.0 L.
Isothermal + ideal gas: change in U = 0 and change in H = 0, so q = -w.
So q = +6.92 kJ absorbed; change in U = change in H = 0.
Example 4 (JEE Advanced): two routes, same states
change in U = 0 by both routes (state function); the reversible route extracts more work.

segments.text: Example three is a J E E Main favourite that rewards spotting the isothermal shortcut.
Two moles of an ideal gas at three hundred kelvin expand isothermally and reversibly from five point zero litres to twenty point zero litres.
<excited>Here is the pro move: isothermal plus ideal gas means the change in internal energy and the change in enthalpy are both zero, so the first law instantly forces q equal to minus w.

The reversible work is minus n R T times the natural log of twenty over five, that is minus two times eight point three one four times three hundred times the log of four, about minus six point nine two kilojoules.
Since q equals minus w, the gas absorbs plus six point nine two kilojoules of heat, while both the internal energy and enthalpy changes stay at zero; every joule absorbed is spent as expansion work.
Example four is the J E E Advanced version: one mole from two litres to eight litres by two different routes between the same two states.
The reversible route gives about minus three thousand four hundred fifty eight joules of work.
The single-step irreversible route against the final pressure gives only about minus one thousand eight hundred seventy one joules.

<whisper>The lesson is the signature of a state function: the change in internal energy is exactly zero by both routes, yet the reversible path extracts strictly more work, which is the conceptual seed of the second law two subtopics later.
Example तीन एक J E E Main का चहेता है जो isothermal shortcut पकड़ने का इनाम देता है।
Two moles ideal gas three hundred kelvin पर isothermally और reversibly five point zero litres से twenty point zero litres तक फैलती है।
<excited>यह रहा pro move: isothermal plus ideal gas का मतलब internal energy और enthalpy दोनों के changes zero हैं, इसलिए first law तुरंत q बराबर minus w कर देता है।
Reversible work है minus n R T into natural log of twenty upon five, यानी minus two into eight point three one four into three hundred into log of four, लगभग minus six point nine two kilojoules।

चूँकि q बराबर minus w है, gas plus six point nine two kilojoules heat absorb करती है, जबकि internal energy और enthalpy दोनों के changes zero रहते हैं; हर absorbed joule expansion work में खर्च हो जाता है।
Example चार J E E Advanced version है: one mole two litres से eight litres तक, एक ही दो states के बीच दो अलग रास्तों से।
Reversible रास्ता लगभग minus three thousand four hundred fifty eight joules work देता है।
Final pressure के खिलाफ़ single-step irreversible रास्ता सिर्फ़ लगभग minus one thousand eight hundred seventy one joules देता है।

<whisper>सबक है state function की पहचान: internal energy का change दोनों रास्तों से ठीक zero है, फिर भी reversible path सख़्ती से ज़्यादा work निकालता है, और यही दो subtopics आगे second law का बीज है।

sections.subtopic: Thermodynamic Terms, First Law, Internal Energy & Enthalpy
sections.title: Pitfalls and pro-tips: signs, R, and delta n-g

board_events.text: The four killer traps
Sign of work: on the system is +, by the system (expansion) is -. If the gas expands, w is negative.
Wrong R: 8.314 J per K per mol for joules; 0.0821 L atm per K per mol only for litre-atmospheres.
Counting solids/liquids in delta n-g: only gaseous moles count. C(s), water(l) are invisible.
Calling q or w a state function: they are PATH functions. Only U, H, T, P, V are state functions.
Pro-tip: the isothermal reflex
For any isothermal ideal-gas process, write change in U = 0 and change in H = 0 on sight, then q = -w.

segments.text: Before we leave the first subtopic, let's inoculate you against the four errors that quietly cost the most marks.

The biggest single error is the sign of work: memorise it from the system's viewpoint, work done on the system is positive, work done by the system in expansion is negative, so if the gas expands, w is negative, full stop.

Second, using the wrong gas constant: eight point three one four for answers in joules, and the zero point zero eight two one value only when you are deliberately working in litre-atmospheres; mixing them is a guaranteed factor-of-a-hundred blunder.
Third, counting solids and liquids in delta n-g: only gaseous moles enter that term, so solid carbon and liquid water are completely invisible to it.
Fourth, calling heat or work a state function: they are path functions, and only internal energy, enthalpy, temperature, pressure and volume are state functions.
<excited>And now the pro-tip that saves whole calculations in the exam hall.
For any isothermal process of an ideal gas, write the change in internal energy and the change in enthalpy as zero on sight, and the first law immediately collapses to q equals minus w.
पहला subtopic छोड़ने से पहले, आपको उन चार गलतियों से बचा देते हैं जो चुपचाप सबसे ज़्यादा marks खा जाती हैं।
सबसे बड़ी अकेली गलती है work का sign: इसे system के नज़रिए से याद रखिए, system पर किया work positive, system द्वारा expansion में किया work negative, तो अगर gas फैलती है, w negative है, बस।

दूसरा, गलत gas constant: joules में answer के लिए eight point three one four, और zero point zero eight two one वाली value सिर्फ़ तब जब आप जानबूझकर litre-atmospheres में काम कर रहे हों; इन्हें मिलाना पक्का factor-of-a-hundred की चूक है।
तीसरा, delta n-g में solids और liquids गिनना: सिर्फ़ gaseous moles उस term में आते हैं, इसलिए solid carbon और liquid water उसके लिए पूरी तरह invisible हैं।
चौथा, heat या work को state function कहना: वे path functions हैं, और सिर्फ़ internal energy, enthalpy, temperature, pressure और volume state functions हैं।
<excited>और अब वो pro-tip जो exam hall में पूरी की पूरी calculations बचा देता है।
किसी भी ideal gas के isothermal process के लिए, internal energy और enthalpy के changes को देखते ही zero लिख दीजिए, और first law तुरंत q बराबर minus w में सिमट जाता है।

sections.subtopic: Thermochemistry, Enthalpy of Reactions & Hess's Law
sections.title: Enthalpy of reaction: exothermic versus endothermic

board_events.text: Thermochemistry = accounting the heat of bonds
Enthalpy of reaction (delta-r H) = heat exchanged at constant pressure when bonds break and form.
Products LOWER than reactants: energy released, EXOTHERMIC, delta-r H is negative.
Everyday: burning a matchstick, neutralising acid with base.
Products HIGHER than reactants: energy absorbed, ENDOTHERMIC, delta-r H is positive.
Everyday: the instant cold pack that turns icy when you snap it.
Enthalpy is a state function (Sub-topic 1). Thermochemistry is just that idea let loose on reactions.

segments.text: In the first subtopic we fixed the rule that enthalpy is a state function, caring only about start and finish; thermochemistry is simply that idea turned loose on chemical reactions.
Every reaction carries an enthalpy of reaction, the heat exchanged at constant pressure as bonds break and new bonds form.
<curious>If the products sit at lower enthalpy than the reactants, energy is released and the reaction is exothermic, so its enthalpy change is negative.
You have felt this many times, burning a matchstick or neutralising acid with base both pour out heat.
If instead the products sit higher, the reaction must be fed energy from outside and is endothermic, with a positive enthalpy change.
The classic picture is the instant cold pack that turns icy the moment you snap it, drinking heat from your hand.
Keep the anchor firmly in mind: because enthalpy is a state function, thermochemistry is not a new principle at all, just careful bookkeeping of heat.
This level diagram captures it: for an exothermic reaction the products settle below the reactants, and the drop is the heat released.
पहले subtopic में हमने यह नियम पक्का किया कि enthalpy एक state function है, जिसे सिर्फ़ start और finish की परवाह है; thermochemistry बस वही idea है जो chemical reactions पर छोड़ दिया गया है।
हर reaction एक enthalpy of reaction रखती है, यानी constant pressure पर वह heat जो bonds टूटने और नए bonds बनने में exchange होती है।
<curious>अगर products, reactants से कम enthalpy पर बैठें, तो energy release होती है और reaction exothermic होती है, तो उसका enthalpy change negative है।
यह आपने कई बार महसूस किया है, माचिस जलाना या acid को base से neutralise करना, दोनों heat उड़ेलते हैं।
अगर इसके बजाय products ऊपर बैठें, तो reaction को बाहर से energy देनी पड़ती है और वह endothermic होती है, positive enthalpy change के साथ।
Classic तस्वीर है instant cold pack जो snap करते ही बर्फ़ जैसा ठंडा हो जाता है, आपके हाथ से heat पीते हुए।
Anchor मज़बूती से याद रखिए: चूँकि enthalpy एक state function है, thermochemistry कोई नया principle है ही नहीं, बस heat का सावधान bookkeeping।
यह level diagram इसे पकड़ लेता है: exothermic reaction के लिए products, reactants से नीचे बैठते हैं, और यह गिरावट ही release हुई heat है।

sections.title: Hess's law and the formation reference table

board_events.text: Hess's law of constant heat summation
Chennai to Delhi: the direct fare must equal the two-leg fare via Nagpur, or you could magic money out of nothing.
One step or several: the total enthalpy change is the same, because H depends only on the endpoints.
Hess's law is the first law wearing chemical clothes — not a new principle.
Power: it gives enthalpies we can never measure directly, like C + half O2 to CO (which always makes some CO2 too).
The formation reference table
Assign zero enthalpy of formation to every element in its most stable form — a sea-level datum.

segments.text: Hess's law of constant heat summation sounds intimidating, so let's meet it through a train ticket.

Picture booking Chennai to Delhi; you can go direct, or break it as Chennai to Nagpur to Delhi, and if the railways price honestly, the two-leg total must equal the direct fare, otherwise you could loop around and magic money out of nothing.

<excited>Hess's law is exactly that honesty rule for enthalpy: whether a reaction runs in one step or as a sum of several, the total enthalpy change is identical, because enthalpy depends only on the endpoints.
So Hess's law is not a new principle at all, it is simply the first law wearing chemical clothes.

And it is enormously useful: it lets us compute the enthalpy of a reaction we can never run cleanly, like carbon plus half an oxygen molecule to carbon monoxide, which stubbornly makes some carbon dioxide too, by adding reactions we can measure.
The same honesty logic hands us a master reference table.

If we agree to assign zero enthalpy of formation to every element in its most stable form, a sea-level datum just like the unmeasurable internal energy of the first subtopic, then every compound gets a single tabulated formation number.
The triangle on the board says it cleanly: the direct route from A to D must equal the sum of the stepwise route through B.
Hess's law of constant heat summation सुनने में डरावना लगता है, तो इसे एक train ticket के ज़रिए मिलते हैं।

Chennai से Delhi की booking सोचिए; आप direct जा सकते हैं, या इसे Chennai to Nagpur to Delhi में तोड़ सकते हैं, और अगर railways ईमानदारी से किराया रखे, तो दो-leg का कुल, direct fare के बराबर होना ही चाहिए, वरना आप घूम-घुमाकर कुछ नहीं से पैसा बना लेते।
<excited>Hess's law enthalpy के लिए बिलकुल वही honesty rule है: reaction चाहे एक step में चले या कई का जोड़ हो, कुल enthalpy change एक जैसा रहता है, क्योंकि enthalpy सिर्फ़ endpoints पर निर्भर है।
तो Hess's law कोई नया principle है ही नहीं, यह बस chemical कपड़े पहने first law है।

और यह बेहद काम का है: यह हमें उस reaction की enthalpy निकालने देता है जिसे हम साफ़ चला ही नहीं सकते, जैसे carbon plus half oxygen molecule to carbon monoxide, जो ज़िद्दी होकर कुछ carbon dioxide भी बना देती है, हम जिन reactions को नाप सकते हैं उन्हें जोड़कर।
वही honesty logic हमें एक master reference table थमा देता है।

अगर हम हर element को उसके सबसे stable रूप में zero enthalpy of formation देना मान लें, एक sea-level datum ठीक पहले subtopic की अनापने वाली internal energy जैसा, तो हर compound को एक अकेला tabulated formation number मिल जाता है।
Board पर बना triangle इसे साफ़ कह देता है: A से D का direct रास्ता, B से होकर stepwise रास्ते के जोड़ के बराबर होना चाहिए।

sections.subtopic: Thermochemistry, Enthalpy of Reactions & Hess's Law
sections.title: The family of standard enthalpy changes

board_events.text: Standard enthalpy changes (1 bar, stated T)
Formation (delta-f H): forming 1 mole of compound from elements in their reference states. Elements = 0.
Combustion (delta-c H): burning 1 mole completely in oxygen. Always negative.
Neutralisation (strong acid + strong base): nearly constant at about -57.1 kJ per mol.
Why constant? The only net reaction is H+ (aq) + OH- (aq) to water (l).
Phase transitions: fusion, vaporisation, sublimation, with sublimation = fusion + vaporisation.
Bond enthalpy: energy to break 1 mole of a bond in the gaseous state; polyatomics use MEAN bond enthalpy.
Lattice enthalpy: separating 1 mole of an ionic solid into gaseous ions (found via Born-Haber).

segments.text: Thermochemistry comes with a small family of named enthalpy changes, all quoted in the standard state of one bar and a stated temperature.

The standard enthalpy of formation is the change when one mole of a compound forms from its elements in their reference states, and by convention every element in its reference state has a formation enthalpy of exactly zero.
The standard enthalpy of combustion is the change when one mole is burnt completely in oxygen, and it is always negative because burning releases heat.
The enthalpy of neutralisation of any strong acid by any strong base is remarkably constant, close to minus fifty seven point one kilojoules per mole.

<curious>Why so constant? Because strong acids and bases are fully ionised, the only net reaction left is a hydrogen ion meeting a hydroxide ion to make water, no matter which acid and base you picked.
Then come the phase-transition enthalpies of fusion, vaporisation and sublimation, and Hess's law ties them together: subliming equals fusing plus vaporising.
Bond enthalpy is the energy to break one mole of a given bond in the gaseous state, and for polyatomic molecules we use a mean value averaged over the molecule.
Finally, lattice enthalpy is the change when one mole of an ionic solid separates into gaseous ions, a quantity we can only reach indirectly through a Born-Haber cycle.
Thermochemistry के साथ named enthalpy changes का एक छोटा परिवार आता है, सब standard state one bar और एक बताए गए temperature पर quoted।

Standard enthalpy of formation वह change है जब एक mole compound अपने elements से उनके reference states में बनता है, और convention से हर element अपने reference state में ठीक zero formation enthalpy रखता है।
Standard enthalpy of combustion वह change है जब एक mole पूरी तरह oxygen में जलता है, और यह हमेशा negative होता है क्योंकि जलना heat release करता है।
किसी भी strong acid की किसी भी strong base से enthalpy of neutralisation उल्लेखनीय रूप से constant होती है, लगभग minus fifty seven point one kilojoules per mole के पास।

<curious>इतनी constant क्यों? क्योंकि strong acids और bases पूरी तरह ionised होते हैं, बचा हुआ अकेला net reaction है एक hydrogen ion का एक hydroxide ion से मिलकर water बनाना, चाहे आपने कोई भी acid और base चुना हो।
फिर आती हैं phase-transition enthalpies fusion, vaporisation और sublimation की, और Hess's law इन्हें जोड़ देता है: subliming बराबर fusing plus vaporising।
Bond enthalpy gaseous state में एक mole किसी bond को तोड़ने की energy है, और polyatomic molecules के लिए हम molecule भर पर औसत की गई mean value लेते हैं।
आखिर में, lattice enthalpy वह change है जब एक mole ionic solid gaseous ions में अलग होता है, एक ऐसी quantity जिस तक हम सिर्फ़ Born-Haber cycle से indirectly पहुँच सकते हैं।

sections.subtopic: Thermochemistry, Enthalpy of Reactions & Hess's Law
sections.title: Three engines: Hess algebra, bond enthalpies, and Born-Haber

board_events.text: Hess algebra: three legal moves
Reverse an equation, reverse the sign of its delta-H.
Multiply an equation by a factor, multiply its delta-H by the same factor; add equations, add their delta-H.
Bond-enthalpy method (gaseous species)
Atomise reactants (cost), then assemble products (release). Count EVERY bond; all species must be gaseous.
Born-Haber loop for an ionic solid MX
Order: sublime metal, ionise it, dissociate half X2, add an electron to X, then lattice forms.
Sign discipline: sublimation, ionisation, dissociation are +; electron gain and lattice formation are -.

segments.text: Hess's law becomes a calculation engine once you learn three legal algebraic moves for combining measured reactions.
First, if you reverse an equation, you reverse the sign of its enthalpy change.
Second, if you multiply an equation by a factor you multiply its enthalpy change by the same factor, and when you add equations you add their enthalpy changes.
The second engine is the bond-enthalpy method, valid for gaseous species.

<curious>Picture it as completely atomising the reactants, which costs the sum of reactant bond enthalpies, then assembling the products, which releases the sum of product bond enthalpies, and remember to count every single bond, all four carbon-hydrogen bonds in methane, both oxygen-hydrogen bonds in water.
The third engine is the Born-Haber cycle, a closed loop for the lattice enthalpy of an ionic solid.
Read it in order: sublime the metal, ionise it, dissociate half a mole of the halogen into atoms, add an electron to that atom, and finally let the gaseous ions collapse into the lattice.
<whisper>The whole battle here is sign discipline: sublimation, ionisation and dissociation are endothermic and positive, while electron gain and lattice formation are exothermic and negative.
Hess's law एक calculation engine बन जाता है जब आप नापी हुई reactions जोड़ने के तीन legal algebraic moves सीख लेते हैं।
पहला, अगर आप कोई equation reverse करते हैं, तो उसकी enthalpy change का sign reverse हो जाता है।
दूसरा, अगर आप किसी equation को किसी factor से multiply करें तो उसकी enthalpy change भी उसी factor से multiply होती है, और जब आप equations जोड़ते हैं तो उनकी enthalpy changes जुड़ जाती हैं।
दूसरा engine है bond-enthalpy method, gaseous species के लिए valid।

<curious>इसे ऐसे सोचिए कि reactants को पूरी तरह atomise करना, जिसकी लागत reactant bond enthalpies का जोड़ है, फिर products को assemble करना, जो product bond enthalpies का जोड़ release करता है, और हर एक bond गिनना मत भूलिए, methane में चारों carbon-hydrogen bonds, water में दोनों oxygen-hydrogen bonds।
तीसरा engine है Born-Haber cycle, किसी ionic solid की lattice enthalpy के लिए एक closed loop।
इसे क्रम में पढ़िए: metal को sublime कीजिए, उसे ionise कीजिए, halogen का आधा mole atoms में dissociate कीजिए, उस atom में एक electron जोड़िए, और आखिर में gaseous ions को lattice में सिमटने दीजिए।
<whisper>यहाँ पूरी लड़ाई sign discipline की है: sublimation, ionisation और dissociation endothermic और positive हैं, जबकि electron gain और lattice formation exothermic और negative।

segments.text: Let's park the thermochemistry formulas on one board for fast recall.
The first master formula computes a reaction enthalpy from tabulated formation enthalpies.
The standard reaction enthalpy equals the sum of stoichiometric coefficient times formation enthalpy over the products, minus the same sum over the reactants.
The second master formula uses bond enthalpies and applies to gaseous species.
The reaction enthalpy equals the sum of bond enthalpies of bonds broken in the reactants, minus the sum of bond enthalpies of bonds formed in the products.

<whisper>Burn this direction alert into memory: the formation formula runs products minus reactants, while the bond-enthalpy formula runs reactants minus products, the exact opposite, because you pay to break what you start with.
A neat Hess consequence links the phase transitions: the enthalpy of sublimation equals the enthalpy of fusion plus the enthalpy of vaporisation.
And the Born-Haber loop for a solid M X sets its formation enthalpy equal to sublimation plus ionisation plus half the dissociation plus electron-gain plus lattice enthalpy.
Thermochemistry के formulas fast recall के लिए एक board पर रख देते हैं।
पहला master formula tabulated formation enthalpies से reaction enthalpy निकालता है।
Standard reaction enthalpy बराबर है products पर stoichiometric coefficient into formation enthalpy का जोड़, minus reactants पर वही जोड़।
दूसरा master formula bond enthalpies इस्तेमाल करता है और gaseous species पर लागू होता है।
Reaction enthalpy बराबर है reactants में टूटे bonds की bond enthalpies का जोड़, minus products में बने bonds की bond enthalpies का जोड़।

<whisper>इस direction alert को memory में जला लीजिए: formation formula products minus reactants चलता है, जबकि bond-enthalpy formula reactants minus products, बिलकुल उल्टा, क्योंकि जो आप शुरू में रखते हैं उसे तोड़ने की कीमत आप चुकाते हैं।
एक साफ़ Hess नतीजा phase transitions को जोड़ता है: enthalpy of sublimation बराबर enthalpy of fusion plus enthalpy of vaporisation।
और solid M X के लिए Born-Haber loop उसकी formation enthalpy को sublimation plus ionisation plus half dissociation plus electron-gain plus lattice enthalpy के बराबर रखता है।

board_events.text: Example 1 (CBSE): hydrogenation of ethene
Given delta-f H: ethene = +52.3, ethane = -84.7, hydrogen = 0 kJ per mol.
Hydrogen, an element in its reference state, contributes zero.
Example 2 (NEET): Hess combination
(i) C + O2 to CO2, delta-H1 = -393.5; (ii) CO + half O2 to CO2, delta-H2 = -283.0 kJ.
Trap: subtracting equation (ii) flips its sign FIRST. Writing -393.5 - 283.0 is the classic error.

segments.text: Example one is a straight C B S E application of the formation formula: the hydrogenation of ethene to ethane.
You are given the formation enthalpies: ethene at plus fifty two point three, ethane at minus eighty four point seven, and hydrogen at zero kilojoules per mole.

Apply products minus reactants: minus eighty four point seven, minus the bracket of plus fifty two point three plus zero, giving minus one hundred thirty seven point zero kilojoules per mole, an exothermic reaction.
Notice that hydrogen, being an element in its reference state, contributes exactly zero to the sum.
Example two is an N E E T speed trap built on Hess combinations.

You are given reaction one, carbon plus oxygen to carbon dioxide at minus three hundred ninety three point five, and reaction two, carbon monoxide plus half an oxygen to carbon dioxide at minus two hundred eighty three point zero kilojoules.

The target, carbon plus half an oxygen to carbon monoxide, is reaction one minus reaction two, so the answer is minus three hundred ninety three point five minus minus two hundred eighty three point zero, which is minus one hundred ten point five kilojoules.

<whisper>Here is the mark-losing trap: subtracting reaction two means flipping its sign first; a student who writes minus three ninety three point five minus two eighty three point zero has effectively added the reverse step twice.
Example एक formation formula का सीधा C B S E application है: ethene का ethane में hydrogenation।
आपको formation enthalpies दी गई हैं: ethene plus fifty two point three पर, ethane minus eighty four point seven पर, और hydrogen zero kilojoules per mole पर।

Products minus reactants लगाइए: minus eighty four point seven, minus plus fifty two point three plus zero का bracket, जो देता है minus one hundred thirty seven point zero kilojoules per mole, एक exothermic reaction।
ध्यान दीजिए hydrogen, अपने reference state में एक element होने के कारण, इस जोड़ में ठीक zero contribute करता है।
Example दो Hess combinations पर बना एक N E E T speed trap है।

आपको reaction एक दी है, carbon plus oxygen to carbon dioxide minus three hundred ninety three point five पर, और reaction दो, carbon monoxide plus half oxygen to carbon dioxide minus two hundred eighty three point zero kilojoules पर।

Target, carbon plus half oxygen to carbon monoxide, reaction एक minus reaction दो है, तो answer है minus three hundred ninety three point five minus minus two hundred eighty three point zero, यानी minus one hundred ten point five kilojoules।

<whisper>यह रहा marks खाने वाला trap: reaction दो को घटाने का मतलब है पहले उसका sign flip करना; जो student minus three ninety three point five minus two eighty three point zero लिखता है उसने असल में reverse step को दो बार जोड़ दिया।

board_events.text: Example 3 (JEE Main): combustion of methane
Example 4 (JEE Advanced): lattice enthalpy of KCl
delta-f = -437; sublimation = +89; ionisation = +419; half dissociation = +122; electron gain = -349.
Solve: -437 = 281 + lattice, so lattice enthalpy = -718 kJ per mol.

segments.text: Example three is a J E E Main bond-enthalpy numerical on the combustion of methane, and it rewards careful bond counting.

The bonds broken in the reactants are four carbon-hydrogen bonds plus two oxygen-double-bond-oxygen bonds, that is four times four hundred fourteen plus two times four hundred ninety eight, giving two thousand six hundred fifty two.

The bonds formed in the products are two carbon-double-bond-oxygen bonds plus four oxygen-hydrogen bonds, that is two times seven hundred ninety nine plus four times four hundred sixty three, giving three thousand four hundred fifty.

The reaction enthalpy is bonds broken minus bonds formed, two thousand six hundred fifty two minus three thousand four hundred fifty, which is minus seven hundred ninety eight kilojoules per mole; note we kept water gaseous, as bond enthalpies demand.
Example four is the J E E Advanced favourite: the lattice enthalpy of potassium chloride from a Born-Haber loop.

You are given the formation enthalpy minus four hundred thirty seven, sublimation plus eighty nine, ionisation plus four hundred nineteen, half the dissociation plus one hundred twenty two, and electron gain minus three hundred forty nine.

Set the formation enthalpy equal to the stepwise sum plus the unknown lattice enthalpy, so minus four hundred thirty seven equals eighty nine plus four hundred nineteen plus one hundred twenty two minus three hundred forty nine plus the lattice term.

<excited>The measurable steps add to two hundred eighty one, so minus four hundred thirty seven equals two hundred eighty one plus the lattice enthalpy, which gives minus seven hundred eighteen kilojoules per mole, and the whole rigor was in the bookkeeping of signs and the half-coefficient.
Example तीन methane के combustion पर एक J E E Main bond-enthalpy numerical है, और यह सावधान bond गिनती का इनाम देता है।

Reactants में टूटे bonds हैं चार carbon-hydrogen bonds plus दो oxygen-double-bond-oxygen bonds, यानी four into four hundred fourteen plus two into four hundred ninety eight, जो देता है two thousand six hundred fifty two।

Products में बने bonds हैं दो carbon-double-bond-oxygen bonds plus चार oxygen-hydrogen bonds, यानी two into seven hundred ninety nine plus four into four hundred sixty three, जो देता है three thousand four hundred fifty।

Reaction enthalpy है bonds broken minus bonds formed, two thousand six hundred fifty two minus three thousand four hundred fifty, यानी minus seven hundred ninety eight kilojoules per mole; ध्यान दीजिए हमने water को gaseous रखा, जैसा bond enthalpies माँगती हैं।
Example चार J E E Advanced का चहेता है: Born-Haber loop से potassium chloride की lattice enthalpy।

आपको दी है formation enthalpy minus four hundred thirty seven, sublimation plus eighty nine, ionisation plus four hundred nineteen, half dissociation plus one hundred twenty two, और electron gain minus three hundred forty nine।

Formation enthalpy को stepwise जोड़ plus unknown lattice enthalpy के बराबर रखिए, तो minus four hundred thirty seven बराबर eighty nine plus four hundred nineteen plus one hundred twenty two minus three hundred forty nine plus lattice term।

<excited>नापी जा सकने वाली steps जुड़कर two hundred eighty one बनती हैं, तो minus four hundred thirty seven बराबर two hundred eighty one plus lattice enthalpy, जो देता है minus seven hundred eighteen kilojoules per mole, और पूरी rigor signs और half-coefficient के bookkeeping में थी।

sections.subtopic: Thermochemistry, Enthalpy of Reactions & Hess's Law
sections.title: Pitfalls and pro-tips: signs, scaling, and directions

board_events.text: Thermochemistry traps
Reversing an equation flips delta-H to minus delta-H. Decide the algebra before plugging numbers.
Scaling: enthalpy is extensive. Double the reaction, double its delta-H.
Bond-enthalpy direction is reactants minus products (opposite to formation), and species must be gaseous.
Elements in their reference state have delta-f H = 0; do not confuse this with the O=O bond enthalpy.
Born-Haber sign chaos: sublimation, ionisation, dissociation +; electron gain, lattice -. Write each sign before summing.
Pro-tip: two formulas, two directions
Formation: products minus reactants. Bond enthalpies: reactants minus products. Mixing them is the top sign error.

segments.text: Let's close the second subtopic by hardening you against its signature mistakes.
The most common slip is forgetting that reversing an equation flips its enthalpy change to the opposite sign, so decide which steps add and which subtract before you ever plug in a number.
Next, remember that enthalpy is extensive: if you double a reaction, you double its enthalpy change; coefficients scale the heat.

Watch the bond-enthalpy direction carefully, it runs reactants minus products, opposite to the formation formula, and every species must be gaseous, so convert solids or liquids with sublimation or vaporisation first.
Do not assign a nonzero formation enthalpy to an element in its reference state, and never confuse the zero formation enthalpy of oxygen gas with the oxygen-double-bond-oxygen bond enthalpy.

<curious>In Born-Haber problems the whole game is sign chaos: sublimation, ionisation and dissociation are positive, while electron gain and lattice formation are negative, so write each step with its sign before you sum.
And here is the single pro-tip that prevents most sign errors in this subtopic.
Two formulas, two directions: formation is products minus reactants, bond enthalpies is reactants minus products, and mixing the two is the number-one source of a lost mark.
दूसरे subtopic को उसकी signature गलतियों से आपको सख़्त बनाकर बंद करते हैं।
सबसे आम चूक है यह भूलना कि equation reverse करने से उसकी enthalpy change उल्टे sign में बदल जाती है, इसलिए कोई number डालने से पहले तय कीजिए कौन सी steps जुड़ेंगी और कौन घटेंगी।
आगे, याद रखिए enthalpy extensive है: अगर आप reaction double करें, तो उसकी enthalpy change double होती है; coefficients heat को scale करते हैं।

Bond-enthalpy direction ध्यान से देखिए, यह reactants minus products चलता है, formation formula से उल्टा, और हर species gaseous होनी चाहिए, इसलिए solids या liquids को पहले sublimation या vaporisation से convert कीजिए।
किसी reference state वाले element को nonzero formation enthalpy मत दीजिए, और oxygen gas की zero formation enthalpy को oxygen-double-bond-oxygen bond enthalpy से कभी मत उलझाइए।

<curious>Born-Haber problems में पूरा खेल sign chaos का है: sublimation, ionisation और dissociation positive हैं, जबकि electron gain और lattice formation negative, इसलिए जोड़ने से पहले हर step को उसके sign के साथ लिखिए।
और यह रहा वो अकेला pro-tip जो इस subtopic की ज़्यादातर sign errors रोक देता है।
दो formulas, दो directions: formation है products minus reactants, bond enthalpies है reactants minus products, और इन दोनों को मिलाना ही एक lost mark की नंबर-वन वजह है।

sections.subtopic: Entropy, Gibbs Free Energy, Spontaneity & the Second/Third Laws
sections.title: Spontaneity and why exothermic is not the whole story

board_events.text: Which way will a reaction go on its own?
A spontaneous process needs no continuous outside push: iron rusting, ice melting, ink spreading in water.
First instinct: spontaneous = exothermic. It breaks immediately.
Ice melting ABSORBS heat yet is spontaneous above zero degrees Celsius.
Dissolving ammonium chloride is endothermic yet happens eagerly — the beaker turns cold.
So energy lowering cannot be the whole story. Nature chases a second prize: disorder.
Energy bookkeeping (first law) counts energy; it cannot by itself predict direction.

segments.text: The first two subtopics taught us to count energy, but neither can answer the most natural question in chemistry: which way will a reaction actually go on its own?
A process that happens by itself, needing no continuous outside push, is called spontaneous, like iron rusting, ice melting on a summer afternoon, or a drop of ink spreading through water.
Your first instinct might be that spontaneous simply means exothermic, since so many natural reactions pour out heat, but that instinct breaks almost immediately.
<curious>Ice melting actually absorbs heat, yet it is perfectly spontaneous above zero degrees Celsius.
And dissolving ammonium chloride in water is endothermic, yet it happens eagerly while the beaker turns cold in your hand.
So lowering the energy cannot be the whole story; nature is clearly chasing a second prize, and that prize is disorder.
In short, the energy bookkeeping of the first law counts energy beautifully but cannot, by itself, tell us the direction of change; we need a new idea.
पहले दो subtopics ने हमें energy गिनना सिखाया, पर कोई भी chemistry का सबसे स्वाभाविक सवाल जवाब नहीं दे सकता: कोई reaction अपने आप किस दिशा में जाएगी?
जो process अपने आप होता है, बिना किसी लगातार बाहरी धक्के के, वह spontaneous कहलाता है, जैसे लोहे का rust होना, गर्मी की दोपहर में बर्फ़ का पिघलना, या पानी में स्याही की बूँद का फैलना।
आपकी पहली instinct हो सकती है कि spontaneous का मतलब बस exothermic है, क्योंकि इतनी सारी natural reactions heat उड़ेलती हैं, पर वह instinct लगभग तुरंत टूट जाती है।
<curious>बर्फ़ का पिघलना असल में heat absorb करता है, फिर भी zero degrees Celsius के ऊपर यह पूरी तरह spontaneous है।
और पानी में ammonium chloride घोलना endothermic है, फिर भी यह बड़े शौक से होता है जबकि beaker आपके हाथ में ठंडा हो जाता है।
तो energy घटाना पूरी कहानी नहीं हो सकती; nature साफ़ तौर पर एक दूसरा इनाम चाहती है, और वह इनाम है disorder।
संक्षेप में, first law का energy bookkeeping energy को खूबसूरती से गिनता है पर अकेले change की दिशा नहीं बता सकता; हमें एक नए idea की ज़रूरत है।

sections.subtopic: Entropy, Gibbs Free Energy, Spontaneity & the Second/Third Laws
sections.title: Entropy as disorder and the second law

board_events.text: Entropy (S) = measure of disorder
More precisely: the number of ways particles and their energy can be arranged (microstates).
A tidy room drifts to mess; a shuffled deck never sorts itself; incense smoke fills the room.
Order of entropy: gas is much greater than liquid, which is greater than solid.
Second law of thermodynamics
In any spontaneous process the total entropy of the universe increases: change in S-universe is positive.
At equilibrium (or ideal reversible change) the total entropy stays put: change in S-universe is zero.

segments.text: So we introduce entropy, written as S, the measure of that disorder nature keeps chasing.
More precisely, entropy counts the number of ways the particles and their energy can be arranged, what physicists call microstates; more arrangements means more entropy.

You already know its everyday face: a tidy hostel room drifts towards mess, a shuffled deck never sorts itself, and incense smoke lit in one corner always spreads to fill the room, because the disordered arrangement is overwhelmingly more probable.
That gives a ranking you must keep at your fingertips: gases have by far the most entropy, liquids less, and rigid ordered solids the least.
Now the second law of thermodynamics delivers the verdict, and it speaks at the scale of the entire universe.
<excited>In any spontaneous process, the total entropy of the universe increases; the change in the universe's entropy is positive, and the arrow of every natural change points that way.
At equilibrium, or for an idealised reversible change, the total entropy holds steady and its change is exactly zero.
The picture ranks it visually: from tightly ordered solid, to looser liquid, to freely scattered gas, entropy climbs steadily to the right.
तो हम entropy पेश करते हैं, S लिखी जाने वाली, उसी disorder का माप जिसे nature पीछा करती रहती है।
ज़्यादा सटीक कहें तो entropy गिनती है कि particles और उनकी energy कितने तरीक़ों से arrange हो सकती हैं, जिन्हें physicists microstates कहते हैं; जितने ज़्यादा arrangements, उतनी ज़्यादा entropy।

इसका रोज़मर्रा का चेहरा आप जानते ही हैं: सलीक़े वाला hostel room अपने आप बिखर जाता है, shuffle किया deck कभी खुद नहीं सजता, और एक कोने में जली अगरबत्ती का धुआँ हमेशा फैलकर पूरे कमरे में भर जाता है, क्योंकि disordered arrangement कहीं ज़्यादा probable है।
इससे एक ranking मिलती है जो आपकी उँगलियों पर होनी चाहिए: gases में सबसे ज़्यादा entropy, liquids में कम, और rigid ordered solids में सबसे कम।
अब second law of thermodynamics फ़ैसला सुनाता है, और यह पूरे universe के पैमाने पर बोलता है।
<excited>किसी भी spontaneous process में, universe की कुल entropy बढ़ती है; universe की entropy का change positive होता है, और हर natural change का तीर उसी ओर इशारा करता है।
Equilibrium पर, या किसी idealised reversible change के लिए, कुल entropy स्थिर रहती है और उसका change ठीक zero होता है।
तस्वीर इसे नज़रों से समझा देती है: कसकर ordered solid से, ढीले liquid तक, और आज़ादी से बिखरे gas तक, entropy दाईं ओर लगातार चढ़ती है।

sections.subtopic: Entropy, Gibbs Free Energy, Spontaneity & the Second/Third Laws
sections.title: Gibbs free energy and the third law

board_events.text: Folding the surroundings into one system quantity
Tracking system + surroundings is clumsy. Chemists defined Gibbs free energy G = H minus T S.
At constant T and P the universe test collapses to one rule: change in G less than zero means spontaneous.
Defining equation: change in G = change in H minus T times change in S — the tug-of-war in symbols.
Also: minus change in G equals the maximum non-expansion (useful) work obtainable.
Third law of thermodynamics
A perfectly ordered pure crystal at zero kelvin has one arrangement, so its entropy is exactly zero.
That datum lets us tabulate ABSOLUTE entropies — unlike U and H, where we only ever had changes.

segments.text: Tracking the entropy of both the system and its surroundings is clumsy, so chemists cleverly folded the surroundings into a single system-only quantity: the Gibbs free energy.
It is defined simply as enthalpy minus temperature times entropy, and its beauty is what it does to the second law.

At constant temperature and pressure, the whole universe's entropy test collapses into one tidy rule about the system alone: if the change in Gibbs energy is less than zero, the process is spontaneous.

<excited>The defining equation, the change in Gibbs energy equals the change in enthalpy minus temperature times the change in entropy, is literally the tug-of-war written in symbols, with temperature as the referee weighting the disorder term.
There is a bonus meaning too: the negative of the change in Gibbs energy equals the maximum useful, non-expansion work you can extract from the process.
Finally the third law gives entropy something the first two laws never gave energy, an absolute zero point.
A perfectly ordered pure crystal at zero kelvin has only one possible arrangement, so its entropy is exactly zero.
That single datum lets us tabulate the absolute entropy of any substance, which is why entropy tables carry real numbers, unlike internal energy and enthalpy where we only ever had changes.
System और उसके surroundings दोनों की entropy track करना बोझिल है, इसलिए chemists ने चतुराई से surroundings को एक अकेली system-only quantity में समेट दिया: Gibbs free energy।
इसे बस enthalpy minus temperature into entropy के रूप में define करते हैं, और इसकी खूबसूरती वह है जो यह second law के साथ करती है।
Constant temperature और pressure पर, पूरे universe का entropy test अकेले system के बारे में एक साफ़ नियम में सिमट जाता है: अगर Gibbs energy का change zero से कम है, तो process spontaneous है।

<excited>Defining equation, Gibbs energy का change बराबर enthalpy का change minus temperature into entropy का change, सचमुच symbols में लिखा वही tug-of-war है, जिसमें temperature disorder term को तौलने वाला referee है।
एक bonus मतलब भी है: Gibbs energy के change का negative, उस process से निकाले जा सकने वाले maximum useful, non-expansion work के बराबर होता है।
आखिर में third law, entropy को वह देता है जो पहले दो laws ने energy को कभी नहीं दिया, एक absolute zero point।
Zero kelvin पर एक perfectly ordered pure crystal के पास सिर्फ़ एक ही संभव arrangement होता है, इसलिए उसकी entropy ठीक zero होती है।

यही अकेला datum हमें किसी भी पदार्थ की absolute entropy tabulate करने देता है, यही वजह है कि entropy tables में असली numbers होते हैं, internal energy और enthalpy के उलट जहाँ हमारे पास सिर्फ़ changes थे।

sections.title: Deriving the Gibbs criterion, the four cases, and the K link

board_events.text: Why change in G less than zero means spontaneous
Start from total entropy positive, with surroundings term equal to minus system enthalpy over T.
Multiply by minus T (positive), the inequality flips: system enthalpy minus T times system entropy is negative.
That left side IS change in G. So change in G less than zero for a spontaneous change.
The four cases of change in G = change in H minus T change in S
Agree (both favour or both oppose): T cannot overturn it. Conflict: T is the referee, tipping at T = delta-H over delta-S.
From change in G to the equilibrium constant
At equilibrium change in G is zero and Q equals K, giving standard change in G = minus R T ln K.

segments.text: Let's see exactly why the Gibbs criterion works, because the derivation is short and illuminating.
Start from the universal test that the total entropy change is positive, and write the surroundings' entropy at constant pressure as minus the system's enthalpy change divided by temperature.

Now multiply the whole inequality by minus the temperature; since temperature is positive, the inequality flips, and we get the system's enthalpy change minus temperature times the system's entropy change is less than zero.
<curious>But that left-hand side is exactly the change in Gibbs energy, so the change in Gibbs energy being less than zero is just the second law rewritten with system-only quantities.
This immediately organises into the famous four cases of the equation change in Gibbs energy equals change in enthalpy minus temperature times change in entropy.

When the two terms agree, both favourable or both unfavourable, temperature cannot overturn the verdict; when they conflict, temperature is the referee, and the tipping point is the crossover temperature, enthalpy change over entropy change.
The same equation reaches all the way to equilibrium and the equilibrium constant.

At equilibrium the drive to change vanishes, so the change in Gibbs energy is zero and the reaction quotient equals the constant, giving the standard change in Gibbs energy equal to minus R T times the natural log of K.
The table on the board freezes the four cases: minus-plus always, minus-minus low temperature, plus-plus high temperature, and plus-minus never.
देखते हैं Gibbs criterion ठीक-ठीक क्यों काम करता है, क्योंकि derivation छोटी और रोशन करने वाली है।
उस universal test से शुरू कीजिए कि कुल entropy का change positive है, और constant pressure पर surroundings की entropy को system के enthalpy change का minus temperature से भाग के रूप में लिखिए।

अब पूरी inequality को minus temperature से multiply कीजिए; चूँकि temperature positive है, inequality पलट जाती है, और हमें मिलता है कि system का enthalpy change minus temperature into system का entropy change, zero से कम है।
<curious>पर वह बायाँ पक्ष ठीक Gibbs energy का change है, तो Gibbs energy के change का zero से कम होना बस second law है जो system-only quantities से दोबारा लिखा गया है।
यह तुरंत उस मशहूर चार cases में सज जाता है, समीकरण Gibbs energy का change बराबर enthalpy का change minus temperature into entropy का change के।

जब दोनों terms सहमत हों, दोनों favourable या दोनों unfavourable, temperature फ़ैसला नहीं पलट सकता; जब वे टकराएँ, temperature referee है, और tipping point है crossover temperature, enthalpy change बटा entropy change।
यही समीकरण equilibrium और equilibrium constant तक पहुँच जाता है।

Equilibrium पर बदलने की चाह ख़त्म हो जाती है, तो Gibbs energy का change zero होता है और reaction quotient constant के बराबर, जो देता है standard Gibbs energy change बराबर minus R T into natural log of K।
Board पर बनी table चार cases जमा देती है: minus-plus हमेशा, minus-minus low temperature, plus-plus high temperature, और plus-minus कभी नहीं।

sections.subtopic: Entropy, Gibbs Free Energy, Spontaneity & the Second/Third Laws
sections.title: Entropy, Gibbs, and the equilibrium toolkit

board_events.text: Spontaneity toolkit
Criterion: change in G negative spontaneous; zero equilibrium; positive non-spontaneous.

segments.text: Here is the compact toolkit for the entire spontaneity subtopic, all on one board for revision.
Entropy change for a reversible heat exchange is the reversible heat divided by temperature, and for a phase transition it is the transition enthalpy divided by the transition temperature.

The second law in working form: the total entropy change is the system part plus the surroundings part, and at constant pressure the surroundings part is minus the system's enthalpy change over temperature.
The Gibbs free energy itself is enthalpy minus temperature times entropy.
For a change at constant temperature, its change is the change in enthalpy minus temperature times the change in entropy.
<whisper>The criterion to burn in: a negative change in Gibbs energy is spontaneous, zero is equilibrium, and positive is non-spontaneous.
The equilibrium link says the standard change in Gibbs energy equals minus R T times the natural log of the equilibrium constant, or with the two point three zero three factor on the base-ten log.
And the crossover temperature, where the change in Gibbs energy passes through zero, is simply the enthalpy change divided by the entropy change, in matching units.
यह रहा पूरे spontaneity subtopic का compact toolkit, revision के लिए एक ही board पर।
Reversible heat exchange के लिए entropy change है reversible heat बटा temperature, और phase transition के लिए यह transition enthalpy बटा transition temperature है।
Second law काम के रूप में: कुल entropy change बराबर system हिस्सा plus surroundings हिस्सा, और constant pressure पर surroundings हिस्सा है minus system का enthalpy change बटा temperature।
Gibbs free energy खुद है enthalpy minus temperature into entropy।
Constant temperature पर किसी change के लिए, उसका change है enthalpy का change minus temperature into entropy का change।
<whisper>याद रखने वाला criterion: negative Gibbs energy change spontaneous है, zero equilibrium, और positive non-spontaneous।
Equilibrium link कहता है कि standard Gibbs energy change बराबर minus R T into equilibrium constant का natural log, या base-ten log पर two point three zero three factor के साथ।
और crossover temperature, जहाँ Gibbs energy का change zero से गुज़रता है, बस enthalpy change बटा entropy change है, मिलती-जुलती units में।

sections.subtopic: Entropy, Gibbs Free Energy, Spontaneity & the Second/Third Laws
sections.title: Computing change in G and the crossover temperature

board_events.text: Example 1 (CBSE): change in G at 298 K
delta-H = -92.4 kJ; delta-S = -198.3 J per K, so -0.1983 kJ per K. Convert units first!
Change in G is negative, so the reaction is spontaneous at 298 K.
Example 2 (NEET): above what T spontaneous?
delta-H = +30.0 kJ, delta-S = +100 J per K: signs conflict, so high-T case (row 3).
Spontaneous above 300 K. Match units (both joules) and read the table — no full delta-G grind.

segments.text: Example one is a clean C B S E computation of the change in Gibbs energy at two hundred ninety eight kelvin.

You are given the enthalpy change as minus ninety two point four kilojoules and the entropy change as minus one hundred ninety eight point three joules per kelvin, which is minus zero point one nine eight three kilojoules per kelvin once you convert, and converting units first is the whole battle.

The change in Gibbs energy is minus ninety two point four minus two hundred ninety eight times minus zero point one nine eight three, which is minus ninety two point four plus fifty nine point one, giving minus thirty three point three kilojoules per mole.
Since the change is negative, the reaction is spontaneous at two hundred ninety eight kelvin.
Example two is an N E E T speed trap asking above what temperature a reaction becomes spontaneous.

The enthalpy change is plus thirty point zero kilojoules and the entropy change is plus one hundred joules per kelvin, so the signs conflict, which is the high-temperature case, row three of the table.
The boundary is the crossover temperature, the enthalpy change over the entropy change, thirty thousand joules over one hundred joules per kelvin, which is three hundred kelvin.
<whisper>So it is spontaneous above three hundred kelvin; convert both to joules to match units, recognise the plus-plus high-temperature case instantly, and skip the full Gibbs energy grind.
Example एक two hundred ninety eight kelvin पर Gibbs energy के change की साफ़ C B S E computation है।

आपको enthalpy change मिला है minus ninety two point four kilojoules, और entropy change minus one hundred ninety eight point three joules per kelvin, जो convert करने पर minus zero point one nine eight three kilojoules per kelvin बनता है, और पहले units convert करना ही पूरी लड़ाई है।

Gibbs energy का change है minus ninety two point four minus two hundred ninety eight into minus zero point one nine eight three, यानी minus ninety two point four plus fifty nine point one, जो देता है minus thirty three point three kilojoules per mole।
चूँकि change negative है, reaction two hundred ninety eight kelvin पर spontaneous है।
Example दो एक N E E T speed trap है जो पूछता है किस temperature के ऊपर reaction spontaneous बनती है।
Enthalpy change है plus thirty point zero kilojoules और entropy change plus one hundred joules per kelvin, तो signs टकराते हैं, यह high-temperature case है, table की row तीन।
Boundary है crossover temperature, enthalpy change बटा entropy change, thirty thousand joules बटा one hundred joules per kelvin, यानी three hundred kelvin।

<whisper>तो यह three hundred kelvin के ऊपर spontaneous है; units मिलाने के लिए दोनों को joules में convert कीजिए, plus-plus high-temperature case तुरंत पहचानिए, और पूरी Gibbs energy की मेहनत छोड़ दीजिए।

sections.subtopic: Entropy, Gibbs Free Energy, Spontaneity & the Second/Third Laws
sections.title: Total entropy, the K link, and temperature dependence

board_events.text: Example 3 (JEE Main): decide by total entropy
350 K, delta-H = -150 kJ, system delta-S = -90 J per K. Surroundings gain entropy from the released heat.
Total = -90 + 428.6 = +338.6 J per K, positive, so spontaneous. Cross-check: change in G = -118.5 kJ.
Example 4 (JEE Advanced): K and the T where K = 1
298 K, standard delta-H = +55.0 kJ, standard delta-S = +175 J per K.
K = 1 when change in G is zero: T = 55000 over 175 = 314 K. Above it, products become favoured.

segments.text: Example three, a J E E Main problem, asks you to decide spontaneity through the total-entropy criterion and then confirm with Gibbs energy.

At three hundred fifty kelvin the enthalpy change is minus one hundred fifty kilojoules while the system's entropy change is minus ninety joules per kelvin, so the system itself becomes more ordered, but the released heat warms the surroundings.

The surroundings' entropy change is minus the enthalpy change over temperature, that is plus one hundred fifty thousand over three hundred fifty, giving plus four hundred twenty eight point six joules per kelvin per mole.

The total is minus ninety plus four hundred twenty eight point six, which is plus three hundred thirty eight point six joules per kelvin, positive and therefore spontaneous; and cross-checking, the change in Gibbs energy comes to minus one hundred eighteen point five kilojoules, the same verdict.
Example four is a J E E Advanced problem chaining the Gibbs-to-K relation with the crossover idea.
At two hundred ninety eight kelvin the standard enthalpy change is plus fifty five point zero kilojoules and the standard entropy change is plus one hundred seventy five joules per kelvin.

The standard change in Gibbs energy is fifty five thousand minus two hundred ninety eight times one hundred seventy five, which is plus two thousand eight hundred fifty joules, and the equilibrium constant is e to the power minus one point one five zero, about zero point three two, reactant-favoured as expected for a positive standard change.

<excited>The constant equals one when the change in Gibbs energy is zero, so the temperature is fifty five thousand over one hundred seventy five, three hundred fourteen kelvin, and above that temperature the standard change turns negative and products finally become favoured.
Example तीन, एक J E E Main problem, आपसे कहता है total-entropy criterion से spontaneity तय कीजिए और फिर Gibbs energy से confirm कीजिए।

Three hundred fifty kelvin पर enthalpy change है minus one hundred fifty kilojoules जबकि system का entropy change minus ninety joules per kelvin, तो system खुद ज़्यादा ordered हो जाता है, पर release हुई heat surroundings को गरम करती है।

Surroundings का entropy change है minus enthalpy change बटा temperature, यानी plus one hundred fifty thousand बटा three hundred fifty, जो देता है plus four hundred twenty eight point six joules per kelvin per mole।

कुल है minus ninety plus four hundred twenty eight point six, यानी plus three hundred thirty eight point six joules per kelvin, positive और इसलिए spontaneous; और cross-check करने पर Gibbs energy का change आता है minus one hundred eighteen point five kilojoules, वही फ़ैसला।
Example चार एक J E E Advanced problem है जो Gibbs-to-K relation को crossover idea से जोड़ता है।
Two hundred ninety eight kelvin पर standard enthalpy change है plus fifty five point zero kilojoules और standard entropy change plus one hundred seventy five joules per kelvin।

Standard Gibbs energy change है fifty five thousand minus two hundred ninety eight into one hundred seventy five, यानी plus two thousand eight hundred fifty joules, और equilibrium constant है e की power minus one point one five zero, लगभग zero point three two, reactant-favoured जैसा positive standard change के लिए उम्मीद थी।

<excited>Constant one के बराबर तब होता है जब Gibbs energy का change zero हो, तो temperature है fifty five thousand बटा one hundred seventy five, three hundred fourteen kelvin, और उस temperature के ऊपर standard change negative हो जाता है और products आख़िरकार favoured बन जाते हैं।

sections.subtopic: Entropy, Gibbs Free Energy, Spontaneity & the Second/Third Laws
sections.title: Pitfalls and pro-tips: units, the surroundings sign, and rate

board_events.text: Spontaneity traps
The kJ/J clash: delta-H is in kJ, delta-S in J. Convert one before using change in G. Number-one error.
Sign of surroundings entropy: it is minus system enthalpy over T. Exothermic gives a POSITIVE surroundings entropy.
Spontaneity is not rate: change in G less than zero says a reaction CAN happen, not that it happens fast.
Diamond to graphite has change in G less than zero, yet takes geological ages.
Third law is for perfect PURE crystals only — not solutions or glassy solids (they keep residual entropy).
Pro-tip: crossover + sanity check
For above/below-T questions jump to T = delta-H over delta-S. A negative standard change in G must give K greater than one.

segments.text: Let's harden you against the mistakes that quietly sink this high-scoring subtopic.

The number-one error is the kilojoule-versus-joule clash: the enthalpy change is almost always in kilojoules while the entropy change is in joules, so you must convert one before using the Gibbs equation.

Next, the sign of the surroundings' entropy: it is minus the system's enthalpy change over temperature, so an exothermic reaction, with a negative enthalpy change, actually gives a positive surroundings entropy; drop that minus sign and your verdict flips.
<curious>Then the deepest conceptual trap: spontaneity is not speed; a negative change in Gibbs energy says a reaction can happen, never that it happens quickly.
The textbook example is diamond turning into graphite, which is spontaneous yet takes geological ages, because thermodynamics answers if, while kinetics answers how fast.
Be careful with the third law too: entropy is zero at zero kelvin only for a perfect, pure crystal, not for solutions or glassy solids, which keep a residual entropy.
And now the pro-tip for speed and sanity.

For any above-or-below-temperature question, jump straight to the crossover temperature, the enthalpy change over the entropy change, and always sanity-check your equilibrium constant, because a negative standard change in Gibbs energy must give a constant greater than one.
इस high-scoring subtopic को डुबाने वाली गलतियों से आपको सख़्त बनाते हैं।
नंबर-वन गलती है kilojoule-बनाम-joule का टकराव: enthalpy change लगभग हमेशा kilojoules में होता है जबकि entropy change joules में, इसलिए Gibbs equation इस्तेमाल करने से पहले एक को convert करना ही होगा।

आगे, surroundings की entropy का sign: यह minus system का enthalpy change बटा temperature है, तो exothermic reaction, negative enthalpy change के साथ, असल में positive surroundings entropy देती है; वह minus sign छोड़ा तो आपका फ़ैसला पलट जाएगा।
<curious>फिर सबसे गहरा conceptual trap: spontaneity speed नहीं है; negative Gibbs energy change कहता है reaction हो सकती है, कभी यह नहीं कि जल्दी होती है।
पाठ्यपुस्तक का उदाहरण है diamond का graphite में बदलना, जो spontaneous है फिर भी भूवैज्ञानिक युगों जितना समय लेता है, क्योंकि thermodynamics 'क्या' का जवाब देता है, जबकि kinetics 'कितनी जल्दी' का।
Third law के साथ भी सावधान रहिए: entropy zero kelvin पर zero सिर्फ़ perfect, pure crystal के लिए है, solutions या glassy solids के लिए नहीं, जो एक residual entropy रखते हैं।
और अब speed और sanity के लिए pro-tip।

किसी भी ऊपर-या-नीचे-temperature सवाल के लिए, सीधे crossover temperature पर जाइए, enthalpy change बटा entropy change, और हमेशा अपने equilibrium constant की sanity-check कीजिए, क्योंकि negative standard Gibbs energy change को constant greater than one देना ही चाहिए।

sections.subtopic: Calorimetry, Thermodynamic Processes & Additional Enthalpy Changes
sections.title: Calorimetry: the bomb versus the coffee-cup

board_events.text: How do we measure the heat of a reaction?
Trap the reaction in an insulated vessel — a calorimeter — and watch the temperature change.
Bomb calorimeter: sealed, rigid steel. Volume cannot change, so no expansion work: the heat is exactly delta-U.
Recall from Sub-topic 1: at constant volume, q at constant V equals change in U.
Coffee-cup calorimeter: open, at atmospheric pressure, so the heat it registers is delta-H.
The instrument literally chooses which quantity you measure — volume-fixed or pressure-fixed.
Convert between them with change in H = change in U plus delta n-g R T.
