segments.text: The final subtopic puts all our machinery to work, and it opens with a very practical question: how do we actually measure the heat of a reaction?
The trick is to trap the reaction inside a well-insulated vessel called a calorimeter and simply watch the temperature change.
The first design is the bomb calorimeter, a sealed rigid steel chamber; because its volume cannot change, no expansion work is done, so the heat it registers is exactly the change in internal energy.
That is precisely the constant-volume result from the first subtopic, where the heat at constant volume equals the change in internal energy.
The second design is the open coffee-cup calorimeter, sitting at atmospheric pressure, so the heat it registers is the change in enthalpy.
<curious>Notice the lovely point: the instrument literally chooses which quantity you measure, fixing the volume gives you internal energy, fixing the pressure gives you enthalpy.
And to move between the two measurements you use the bridge from the first subtopic, the change in enthalpy equals the change in internal energy plus delta n-g times R T.
The picture contrasts them: the rigid sealed bomb on the left for internal energy, the open cup on the right for enthalpy.
आख़िरी subtopic हमारी सारी machinery को काम में लगाता है, और यह एक बहुत practical सवाल से खुलता है: हम असल में किसी reaction की heat कैसे नापते हैं?
तरकीब यह है कि reaction को एक अच्छी तरह insulated बर्तन में फँसा दीजिए जिसे calorimeter कहते हैं, और बस temperature change देखते रहिए।
पहला design है bomb calorimeter, एक sealed rigid steel chamber; चूँकि इसका volume बदल नहीं सकता, कोई expansion work नहीं होता, इसलिए यह जो heat दर्ज करता है वह ठीक internal energy का change है।
यह ठीक पहले subtopic का constant-volume नतीजा है, जहाँ constant volume पर heat, internal energy के change के बराबर है।
दूसरा design है खुला coffee-cup calorimeter, atmospheric pressure पर बैठा, इसलिए यह जो heat दर्ज करता है वह enthalpy का change है।
<curious>यह प्यारी बात देखिए: instrument सचमुच चुनता है कि आप कौन सी quantity नापेंगे, volume fix करने पर internal energy, pressure fix करने पर enthalpy।
और दोनों measurements के बीच जाने के लिए आप पहले subtopic का bridge इस्तेमाल करते हैं, enthalpy का change बराबर internal energy का change plus delta n-g into R T।
तस्वीर इनका फ़र्क़ दिखाती है: बाईं ओर internal energy के लिए rigid sealed bomb, दाईं ओर enthalpy के लिए खुला cup।

sections.title: The four idealised processes of a gas

board_events.text: Four rules of a game — each freezes one variable
ISOTHERMAL: temperature fixed (cylinder in a water bath). Heat flows freely to hold T.
ADIABATIC: no heat crosses (q = 0). The gas cools on expansion, heats on compression.
A diesel engine compressing air until it is hot enough to ignite fuel is nearly adiabatic.
ISOBARIC: pressure fixed (a free weighted piston). Gas expands or contracts as it is heated.
ISOCHORIC: volume fixed (piston locked, w = 0). All heat goes straight into internal energy.
For an ideal gas, change in U and change in H depend only on change in T — never on the path.

segments.text: The second practical question is: what are the standard ways a gas can change state? Think of four rules of a game, each one freezing a different variable.
In an isothermal change the temperature is held fixed, as if the cylinder sits in a large water bath, and heat flows freely in or out to keep the temperature constant.
In an adiabatic change no heat crosses the boundary at all, so the gas can only change its energy by doing or receiving work; it cools on expansion and heats on compression.
The vivid example is a diesel engine compressing air until it is hot enough to ignite the fuel, which is very nearly adiabatic.
In an isobaric change the pressure is held fixed, imagine a free weighted piston, and the gas simply expands or contracts as it is heated or cooled.
In an isochoric change the volume is locked, so no work is done and every joule of heat goes straight into the internal energy.
<excited>And here is the unifying gift for an ideal gas: the changes in internal energy and enthalpy depend only on the temperature change, never on which of these paths you took.
The P V diagram shows all four fanning out from a common point, with the adiabatic falling more steeply than the isothermal.
दूसरा practical सवाल है: किसी gas के state बदलने के standard तरीक़े क्या हैं? एक खेल के चार नियम सोचिए, हर एक अलग variable को जमा देता है।
Isothermal change में temperature fix रखा जाता है, मानो cylinder एक बड़े water bath में बैठा हो, और temperature constant रखने के लिए heat आज़ादी से अंदर-बाहर बहती है।
Adiabatic change में कोई heat boundary पार करती ही नहीं, इसलिए gas सिर्फ़ work करके या पाकर अपनी energy बदल सकती है; यह expansion पर ठंडी होती है और compression पर गरम।
जीवंत उदाहरण है diesel engine जो हवा को तब तक compress करता है जब तक वह fuel जलाने लायक गरम न हो जाए, जो लगभग पूरी तरह adiabatic है।
Isobaric change में pressure fix रखा जाता है, एक free weighted piston सोचिए, और gas गरम या ठंडा होने पर बस फैलती या सिकुड़ती है।
Isochoric change में volume lock होता है, इसलिए कोई work नहीं होता और heat का हर joule सीधे internal energy में चला जाता है।
<excited>और यह रहा ideal gas के लिए जोड़ने वाला तोहफ़ा: internal energy और enthalpy के changes सिर्फ़ temperature change पर निर्भर करते हैं, कभी इस पर नहीं कि आपने इनमें से कौन सा path लिया।
P V diagram चारों को एक common point से फैलते दिखाता है, जिसमें adiabatic, isothermal से ज़्यादा तेज़ी से गिरता है।

sections.subtopic: Calorimetry, Thermodynamic Processes & Additional Enthalpy Changes
sections.title: Enthalpy of solution: the lattice-hydration tug-of-war

board_events.text: What happens, energetically, when something dissolves?
Dissolving an ionic solid is a tug-of-war between two steps.
Step 1: the crystal lattice must be pulled apart — costs energy (lattice enthalpy, endothermic).
Step 2: the freed ions are surrounded and stabilised by water — releases energy (hydration, exothermic).
Enthalpy of solution = the NET of the two: lattice enthalpy plus hydration enthalpy.
Lattice-breaking wins: dissolving cools the water — the instant COLD pack (ammonium nitrate).
Hydration wins: the solution warms — a HAND warmer (calcium chloride).

segments.text: The third practical question is the most tactile: what happens, energetically, when something dissolves?
Dissolving an ionic solid is a genuine tug-of-war between two competing steps.
In the first step the crystal lattice has to be pulled completely apart, and that costs energy; it is the lattice enthalpy, and it is endothermic.
In the second step the freed ions are surrounded and stabilised by water molecules, and that releases energy; it is the hydration enthalpy, and it is exothermic.
<curious>The enthalpy of solution is simply the net of these two, the lattice enthalpy plus the hydration enthalpy, and whichever wins decides what you feel.
When lattice-breaking wins, dissolving actually cools the water, and that is exactly how an instant cold pack of ammonium nitrate works.
When hydration wins, the solution warms up instead, which is the principle behind a calcium chloride hand warmer.

The cycle on the board shows it as a Hess triangle: solid to gaseous ions costs the positive lattice term, gaseous ions to aqueous releases the negative hydration term, and the dashed net is the enthalpy of solution.
तीसरा practical सवाल सबसे स्पर्शनीय है: जब कुछ घुलता है, तो energy के लिहाज़ से क्या होता है?
किसी ionic solid को घोलना दो प्रतिस्पर्धी steps के बीच सच्चा tug-of-war है।
पहले step में crystal lattice को पूरी तरह अलग करना पड़ता है, और उसमें energy खर्च होती है; यह lattice enthalpy है, और यह endothermic है।
दूसरे step में आज़ाद हुए ions को water molecules घेरकर stabilise करते हैं, और उसमें energy release होती है; यह hydration enthalpy है, और यह exothermic है।
<curious>Enthalpy of solution बस इन दोनों का net है, lattice enthalpy plus hydration enthalpy, और जो जीतता है वही तय करता है आप क्या महसूस करते हैं।
जब lattice-breaking जीतता है, घुलना असल में पानी को ठंडा करता है, और यही ठीक-ठीक ammonium nitrate वाले instant cold pack का काम करने का तरीक़ा है।
जब hydration जीतता है, solution गरम हो जाता है, जो calcium chloride hand warmer के पीछे का सिद्धांत है।

Board पर बना cycle इसे एक Hess triangle के रूप में दिखाता है: solid से gaseous ions में positive lattice term खर्च होता है, gaseous ions से aqueous में negative hydration term release होता है, और dashed net ही enthalpy of solution है।

sections.subtopic: Calorimetry, Thermodynamic Processes & Additional Enthalpy Changes
sections.title: Three derivations: adiabatic work, the bomb, and the solution cycle

board_events.text: Adiabatic work
q = 0, so the first law collapses to change in U = w. And change in U = n C-v times change in T.
With no heat allowed in, expansion work is spent from internal energy, so the gas cools.
Bomb-calorimeter measurement
Burn a known mass in excess oxygen; the fixed volume makes the measured heat equal to change in U.
Find the calorimeter's heat capacity beforehand by burning a substance of known change in U; report delta-H via delta n-g R T.
Enrichments: Trouton and Kirchhoff
Trouton: molar entropy of vaporisation is roughly constant. Kirchhoff: reaction enthalpy drifts with temperature via delta C-p.

segments.text: Let's tie the subtopic together with three short derivations, starting with adiabatic work.

Because no heat crosses in an adiabatic change, the first law collapses to the change in internal energy equalling the work, and since for an ideal gas the internal energy change is n times the constant-volume heat capacity times the temperature change, the work is exactly that.
The physical reading is clean: with no heat allowed in, the only way the gas can do expansion work on the surroundings is to spend its own internal energy, so it necessarily cools.
The second derivation is the bomb-calorimeter measurement.
A known mass is burnt in excess oxygen, and because the volume is fixed, the heat that raises the temperature of the bomb-and-water assembly is exactly the change in internal energy.
You find the calorimeter's heat capacity beforehand by burning a substance of known internal energy change, and if you want the enthalpy you apply the delta n-g R T conversion.
Finally two enrichments worth knowing by name.

<curious>Trouton's rule says the molar entropy of vaporisation at the normal boiling point is roughly constant for many liquids, while Kirchhoff's equation tells you how a reaction enthalpy drifts with temperature through the difference in heat capacities.
इस subtopic को तीन छोटी derivations से जोड़ते हैं, adiabatic work से शुरू करते हुए।

चूँकि adiabatic change में कोई heat पार नहीं करती, first law सिमटकर internal energy का change बराबर work बन जाता है, और चूँकि ideal gas के लिए internal energy change है n into constant-volume heat capacity into temperature change, work ठीक वही है।
Physical समझ साफ़ है: जब heat अंदर आने की इजाज़त नहीं, gas surroundings पर expansion work करने का अकेला तरीक़ा है अपनी internal energy खर्च करना, इसलिए यह ज़रूरी तौर पर ठंडी होती है।
दूसरी derivation है bomb-calorimeter measurement।
एक known mass excess oxygen में जलाया जाता है, और चूँकि volume fix है, जो heat bomb-और-water assembly का temperature बढ़ाती है वह ठीक internal energy का change है।
आप calorimeter की heat capacity पहले से known internal energy change वाला पदार्थ जलाकर निकालते हैं, और अगर enthalpy चाहिए तो delta n-g R T conversion लगाते हैं।
आख़िर में दो enrichments जिन्हें नाम से जानना अच्छा है।

<curious>Trouton's rule कहता है कि normal boiling point पर molar entropy of vaporisation कई liquids के लिए लगभग constant होती है, जबकि Kirchhoff's equation बताता है कि reaction enthalpy temperature के साथ heat capacities के अंतर के ज़रिए कैसे खिसकती है।

sections.title: Calorimetry, the four processes, and Poisson relations

board_events.text: Applications toolkit
Four processes (ideal gas), work done ON the system:

board_events.latex: w_{\text{iso}} = -nRT\ln\dfrac{V_2}{V_1}, \quad w_{\text{adia}} = nC_V\Delta T, \quad w_{\text{isobar}} = -nR\Delta T, \quad w_{\text{isochor}} = 0

segments.text: Here is the applications toolkit for the last subtopic, gathered for quick recall.
Calorimetry starts from heat equals heat capacity times temperature change, or mass times specific heat times temperature change.

In a bomb, the constant-volume heat is the change in internal energy and equals minus the calorimeter heat capacity times its temperature rise, while a coffee-cup gives the change in enthalpy directly.
The four ideal-gas processes each have a work expression, all written for work done on the system.

Isothermal work is minus n R T times the log of the volume ratio, adiabatic work is n times the constant-volume heat capacity times the temperature change, isobaric work is minus n R times the temperature change, and isochoric work is simply zero.

For a reversible adiabatic change the Poisson relations hold: pressure times volume to the gamma is constant, temperature times volume to gamma minus one is constant, and pressure to one minus gamma times temperature to the gamma is constant.
The enthalpy of solution is the lattice enthalpy plus the hydration enthalpy, the tug-of-war in one line.
And Trouton's rule notes that the molar entropy of vaporisation at the boiling point sits near eighty five to eighty eight joules per kelvin per mole for many liquids.
यह रहा आख़िरी subtopic का applications toolkit, quick recall के लिए इकट्ठा।
Calorimetry शुरू होती है heat बराबर heat capacity into temperature change से, या mass into specific heat into temperature change से।
Bomb में, constant-volume heat, internal energy का change है और बराबर है minus calorimeter heat capacity into उसका temperature rise, जबकि coffee-cup सीधे enthalpy का change देता है।
चारों ideal-gas processes में से हर एक का एक work expression है, सब system पर किए गए work के लिए लिखे गए।

Isothermal work है minus n R T into volume ratio का log, adiabatic work है n into constant-volume heat capacity into temperature change, isobaric work है minus n R into temperature change, और isochoric work बस zero है।

Reversible adiabatic change के लिए Poisson relations लागू होते हैं: pressure into volume to the gamma constant, temperature into volume to gamma minus one constant, और pressure to one minus gamma into temperature to the gamma constant।
Enthalpy of solution है lattice enthalpy plus hydration enthalpy, एक लाइन में वही tug-of-war।
और Trouton's rule बताता है कि boiling point पर molar entropy of vaporisation कई liquids के लिए eighty five से eighty eight joules per kelvin per mole के पास बैठती है।

sections.subtopic: Calorimetry, Thermodynamic Processes & Additional Enthalpy Changes
sections.title: Bomb calorimetry and the enthalpy of solution

board_events.text: Example 1 (CBSE): bomb calorimeter
Burn 0.50 g of fuel; heat capacity 8.2 kJ per K; temperature rises 1.20 K. Constant volume gives change in U.
Negative — combustion is exothermic; the bomb gives change in U, not change in H, because V is fixed.
Example 2 (NEET): enthalpy of solution of NaCl
lattice enthalpy = +788 (dissociation); hydration enthalpy = -784 kJ per mol.
Slightly endothermic, so NaCl very mildly COOLS the water. Use lattice in its positive (dissociation) sense.

segments.text: Example one is a C B S E bomb-calorimeter numerical that tests whether you know you are measuring internal energy.

You burn zero point five zero grams of a fuel in a bomb of heat capacity eight point two kilojoules per kelvin, and the temperature rises by one point two zero kelvin, and since the volume is fixed the measured heat is the change in internal energy.

That change is minus eight point two times one point two zero, which is minus nine point eight four kilojoules for zero point five zero grams, and dividing gives minus nineteen point seven kilojoules per gram.
The sign is negative because combustion is exothermic, and remember the bomb gives you the change in internal energy, not enthalpy, precisely because the volume is held fixed.
Example two is an N E E T solution-enthalpy problem for sodium chloride.
You are given the lattice enthalpy as plus seven hundred eighty eight kilojoules per mole in its dissociation sense, and the hydration enthalpy as minus seven hundred eighty four.
The enthalpy of solution is their sum, seven hundred eighty eight plus minus seven hundred eighty four, which is plus four kilojoules per mole.

<whisper>Since it is slightly positive, dissolving sodium chloride very mildly cools the water, and the key is to use the lattice value in its positive dissociation sense so the cycle balances; flipping its sign gives a wildly wrong strongly exothermic answer.
Example एक एक C B S E bomb-calorimeter numerical है जो जाँचता है कि आप जानते हैं कि आप internal energy नाप रहे हैं।

आप zero point five zero grams fuel को eight point two kilojoules per kelvin heat capacity वाले bomb में जलाते हैं, और temperature one point two zero kelvin बढ़ता है, और चूँकि volume fix है, नापी गई heat internal energy का change है।

वह change है minus eight point two into one point two zero, यानी minus nine point eight four kilojoules zero point five zero grams के लिए, और भाग देने पर मिलता है minus nineteen point seven kilojoules per gram।
Sign negative है क्योंकि combustion exothermic है, और याद रखिए bomb आपको internal energy का change देता है, enthalpy का नहीं, ठीक इसलिए कि volume fix रखा गया है।
Example दो sodium chloride के लिए एक N E E T solution-enthalpy problem है।
आपको lattice enthalpy दी है plus seven hundred eighty eight kilojoules per mole उसके dissociation sense में, और hydration enthalpy minus seven hundred eighty four।
Enthalpy of solution इनका जोड़ है, seven hundred eighty eight plus minus seven hundred eighty four, यानी plus four kilojoules per mole।

<whisper>चूँकि यह थोड़ा positive है, sodium chloride घोलना पानी को बहुत हल्का ठंडा करता है, और चाबी यह है कि lattice value को उसके positive dissociation sense में लीजिए ताकि cycle balance हो; उसका sign flip करने पर बुरी तरह ग़लत, ज़ोरदार exothermic answer मिलता है।

sections.subtopic: Calorimetry, Thermodynamic Processes & Additional Enthalpy Changes
sections.title: Adiabatic expansion and the Poisson relation

board_events.text: Example 3 (JEE Main): adiabatic cooling
2 mol monoatomic gas (C-v = three-halves R), adiabatic, cools 400 K to 300 K. So q = 0.
Even on an adiabatic path, change in U follows n C-v change in T and change in H follows n C-p change in T.
Example 4 (JEE Advanced): Poisson expansion
1 mol monoatomic (gamma = five-thirds), 300 K, 1.00 atm to 0.25 atm, reversible adiabatic.

segments.text: Example three is a J E E Main adiabatic problem where the whole trick is that internal energy and enthalpy still follow their temperature formulas.

Two moles of a monoatomic gas with a constant-volume heat capacity of three-halves R expand adiabatically, cooling from four hundred kelvin to three hundred kelvin, and because the process is adiabatic the heat is zero.

The change in internal energy is n times the constant-volume heat capacity times the temperature change, two times twelve point four seven times minus one hundred, which is minus two thousand four hundred ninety four joules, and that also equals the work.

The change in enthalpy is n times the constant-pressure heat capacity times the temperature change, two times twenty point seven nine times minus one hundred, which is minus four thousand one hundred fifty seven joules.
The catch to remember: even on an adiabatic path, the internal energy change follows n C-v times the temperature change and the enthalpy change follows n C-p times the temperature change.

Example four is the J E E Advanced Poisson problem: one mole of a monoatomic gas with gamma equal to five-thirds at three hundred kelvin expands reversibly and adiabatically from one point zero zero atmosphere to zero point two five atmosphere.
Using the Poisson relation, the final temperature is three hundred times zero point two five raised to the power zero point four zero, giving about one hundred seventy two point three kelvin.

<excited>And the work is n times the constant-volume heat capacity times the temperature change, about minus one point five nine kilojoules, so the gas does roughly one point five nine kilojoules of work while cooling sharply, and the rigor lay in pairing the correct Poisson exponent with the work expression.
Example तीन एक J E E Main adiabatic problem है जहाँ पूरी तरकीब यह है कि internal energy और enthalpy अब भी अपने temperature formulas ही follow करते हैं।

Three-halves R constant-volume heat capacity वाली monoatomic gas के two moles adiabatically फैलते हैं, four hundred kelvin से three hundred kelvin तक ठंडे होते हुए, और चूँकि process adiabatic है, heat zero है।

Internal energy का change है n into constant-volume heat capacity into temperature change, two into twelve point four seven into minus one hundred, यानी minus two thousand four hundred ninety four joules, और यही work के भी बराबर है।
Enthalpy का change है n into constant-pressure heat capacity into temperature change, two into twenty point seven nine into minus one hundred, यानी minus four thousand one hundred fifty seven joules।
याद रखने वाली बात: adiabatic path पर भी, internal energy change n C-v into temperature change follow करता है और enthalpy change n C-p into temperature change।

Example चार J E E Advanced Poisson problem है: five-thirds gamma वाली monoatomic gas का one mole three hundred kelvin पर reversibly और adiabatically one point zero zero atmosphere से zero point two five atmosphere तक फैलता है।
Poisson relation इस्तेमाल करने पर, final temperature है three hundred into zero point two five की power zero point four zero, जो देता है लगभग one hundred seventy two point three kelvin।

<excited>और work है n into constant-volume heat capacity into temperature change, लगभग minus one point five nine kilojoules, तो gas लगभग one point five nine kilojoules work करती है जबकि तेज़ी से ठंडी होती है, और rigor सही Poisson exponent को work expression से जोड़ने में थी।

sections.subtopic: Calorimetry, Thermodynamic Processes & Additional Enthalpy Changes
sections.title: Pitfalls and pro-tips: bomb versus cup, adiabatic versus isothermal

board_events.text: Applications traps
Bomb (constant V) gives change in U; coffee-cup (constant P) gives change in H. Do not forget the delta n-g R T conversion.
Adiabatic is NOT isothermal: adiabatic means q = 0 (T changes); isothermal means change in T = 0 (heat flows).
Swapping the two inverts every sign in the problem.
Sign of lattice enthalpy: use the positive dissociation value so the lattice-hydration cycle balances.
Free expansion: external pressure zero, so w = 0; for an ideal gas change in U = 0, so change in T = 0 and q = 0.
Pro-tip: freeze the variable, then jump
Isothermal freezes T, adiabatic freezes heat, isobaric freezes P, isochoric freezes V. Then change in U = n C-v change in T always.

segments.text: Let's close the chapter's applications with the traps that decide marks in the exam.

First, keep the calorimeters straight: the bomb at constant volume gives you the change in internal energy, the coffee-cup at constant pressure gives you the change in enthalpy, and do not forget the delta n-g R T conversion when moving between them.

Second, and most damaging, adiabatic is not isothermal: adiabatic means the heat is zero while the temperature changes, whereas isothermal means the temperature change is zero while heat flows freely.
Swapping those two definitions inverts essentially every sign in the problem, so be ruthless about which one you are in.
Third, in a solution-enthalpy cycle use the lattice enthalpy in its positive dissociation sense so the lattice-and-hydration cycle balances correctly.

Fourth, remember the free-expansion edge case: with zero external pressure the work is zero, and for an ideal gas the internal energy change is zero, so the temperature change and the heat are zero as well.
<excited>And here is the chapter-closing pro-tip that turns process problems into one-liners.

Identify the process by what it freezes, isothermal freezes temperature, adiabatic freezes heat, isobaric freezes pressure, isochoric freezes volume, and then for any ideal-gas path jump straight to internal energy change equals n times the constant-volume heat capacity times the temperature change.
Chapter के applications को उन traps से बंद करते हैं जो exam में marks तय करते हैं।

पहला, calorimeters को साफ़ रखिए: constant volume पर bomb आपको internal energy का change देता है, constant pressure पर coffee-cup enthalpy का change, और इनके बीच जाते समय delta n-g R T conversion मत भूलिए।
दूसरा, और सबसे नुक़सानदेह, adiabatic isothermal नहीं है: adiabatic का मतलब heat zero जबकि temperature बदलता है, जबकि isothermal का मतलब temperature change zero जबकि heat आज़ादी से बहती है।
इन दोनों definitions को उलटने से problem का लगभग हर sign पलट जाता है, इसलिए इस बारे में बेरहम रहिए कि आप किसमें हैं।
तीसरा, solution-enthalpy cycle में lattice enthalpy को उसके positive dissociation sense में लीजिए ताकि lattice-और-hydration cycle सही balance हो।
चौथा, free-expansion edge case याद रखिए: zero external pressure पर work zero, और ideal gas के लिए internal energy change zero, तो temperature change और heat भी zero।
<excited>और यह रहा chapter-closing pro-tip जो process problems को one-liners बना देता है।

Process को इससे पहचानिए कि वह क्या freeze करता है, isothermal temperature, adiabatic heat, isobaric pressure, isochoric volume, और फिर किसी भी ideal-gas path के लिए सीधे internal energy change बराबर n into constant-volume heat capacity into temperature change पर जाइए।

board_events.text: Last-minute quick recall
Signs: 'on is plus, by is minus' for work. q positive = heat in.
State functions U, H, T, P, V care only about endpoints; path functions q, w care about the route. Cyclic: change in U = 0.
R rule: joules want 8.314; litre-atm wants 0.0821. Delta n-g: gases only.
Directions: formation is products minus reactants; bond enthalpies is reactants minus products. Reverse a reaction, reverse the sign.
Gibbs: enthalpy pulls down, entropy pulls up, T is the referee. Four cases: (neg,pos) always, (neg,neg) low T, (pos,pos) high T, (pos,neg) never.
Exothermic warms the surroundings, giving a positive surroundings entropy. Change in G tells you IF, not how fast.
Bomb = box = change in U; open cup = change in H. Adiabatic kills q; isothermal kills change in T. Cold pack = endothermic dissolving.

segments.text: Finally, the last-minute cheat sheet, the one-liners to carry into the exam hall; pure recall, nothing new.
For work signs, chant on is plus, by is minus, and a positive q always means heat flowing into the system.

Internal energy, enthalpy, temperature, pressure and volume are state functions that care only about the endpoints, while heat and work are path functions, and over any cycle the internal energy change is zero.
For the gas constant, joules want eight point three one four while litre-atmospheres want zero point zero eight two one, and delta n-g counts gaseous moles only.
For the two thermochemistry directions, formation runs products minus reactants and bond enthalpies run reactants minus products, and whenever you reverse a reaction you reverse the sign.

For Gibbs energy, enthalpy pulls down, entropy pulls up, and temperature is the referee, with the four cases fixed: minus-plus always, minus-minus low temperature, plus-plus high temperature, plus-minus never.
Remember that an exothermic reaction warms the surroundings and so gives a positive surroundings entropy, and that the change in Gibbs energy tells you whether, never how fast.

<excited>And the calorimetry mnemonics: bomb equals box equals internal energy, an open cup gives enthalpy, adiabatic kills the heat while isothermal kills the temperature change, and a cold pack is simply endothermic dissolving. That is the whole chapter in your pocket.
आख़िर में, last-minute cheat sheet, exam hall में ले जाने वाले one-liners; शुद्ध recall, कुछ नया नहीं।
Work के signs के लिए दोहराइए 'on is plus, by is minus', और positive q का मतलब हमेशा system में heat आना।

Internal energy, enthalpy, temperature, pressure और volume state functions हैं जिन्हें सिर्फ़ endpoints की परवाह है, जबकि heat और work path functions हैं, और किसी भी cycle पर internal energy का change zero होता है।
Gas constant के लिए, joules को चाहिए eight point three one four जबकि litre-atmospheres को zero point zero eight two one, और delta n-g सिर्फ़ gaseous moles गिनता है।
दो thermochemistry directions के लिए, formation चलता है products minus reactants और bond enthalpies चलते हैं reactants minus products, और जब भी आप reaction reverse करें sign reverse कीजिए।
Gibbs energy के लिए, enthalpy नीचे खींचती है, entropy ऊपर, और temperature referee है, चार cases तय: minus-plus हमेशा, minus-minus low temperature, plus-plus high temperature, plus-minus कभी नहीं।
याद रखिए exothermic reaction surroundings को गरम करती है और इसलिए positive surroundings entropy देती है, और Gibbs energy का change बताता है 'क्या', कभी 'कितनी जल्दी' नहीं।

<excited>और calorimetry के mnemonics: bomb बराबर box बराबर internal energy, खुला cup enthalpy देता है, adiabatic heat को मारता है जबकि isothermal temperature change को, और cold pack बस endothermic dissolving है। यही रहा पूरा chapter आपकी जेब में।
